papers.title: Spectrally Routed Diffusion Policy for Multi-Task Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based policies have achieved strong performance on single-task robotic manipulation. However, a single model trained jointly on multiple tasks consistently underperforms the per-task specialists trained on the same demonstrations. We focus on two challenges. First, the convolutional encoders commonly used in diffusion-based policies produce visual conditions that are not discriminative enough. Second, gradients from incompatible action modes update the shared denoiser's dense parameters along the same directions, causing destructive interference during joint training. To address both, we propose SR-DP (Spectrally Routed Diffusion Policy). A frozen VGGT encoder with a spatial-compression adapter produces compact multi-scale semantic-geometric tokens, a task-discriminative visual condition for tasks that share a workspace. We first train the denoiser as a standard diffusion policy, then decompose selected linear layers by SVD into a frozen basis of orthogonal rank-one experts, adapted through spectral routing and Householder input rotations. On six RoboTwin tasks, SR-DP averages a 68.4% success rate, surpassing multi-task VO-DP by 21.8 points and the strongest per-task baseline by 3.8 points. On four real-world bimanual tasks, Stage 2 reaches a 43.0% average success rate and improves over Stage 1 by 19.0 points.

papers.title: CogniLife: Continuous Cognitive Distillation for Deployed Multi-Expert Agent Marketplaces
papers.abstract: Multi-expert agent marketplaces -- where creators publish domain-specific AI experts for end users to consult -- are an emerging deployment pattern for language technology. A published expert can receive many requests yet little evidence about its creator, who remains active elsewhere: the cold-expert problem. We frame continuous cognitive distillation as converting attributed creator observations into revisable decision rules, communication patterns, and domain procedures. CogniLife proposes a cross-expert attribution design for this problem, with Creator Profiles for transferable creator patterns and Expert Journals for listing-specific knowledge; this design is not yet implemented or evaluated. A deployed platform partially realizes the surrounding lifecycle through creator-authorized authoring, capability-owned proposal filtering, and reversible consolidation of eligible owner-scoped memory. On ProfyBench-v1, an 85-task offline benchmark built from replay seeds and controlled internal tests, the Profy Full configuration as a whole achieves a mean overall score of 4.65/5 from the primary LLM judge, compared with 4.01 for Raw LLM and 4.28 for Expert Prompt, with the largest gains in completeness, specificity, and missing-information tasks. These configuration-level scores do not test cold-expert mitigation, cross-expert transfer, or longitudinal distillation.

papers.title: 3DGS-VBench+ and 3DGSV-Assessor: A Multi-Dimensional Subjective Benchmark and a Reference-Flexible Objective Model for 3D Gaussian Splatting Video Quality Assessment
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables real-time novel view synthesis (NVS), but its heavy storage makes compression essential, and both training and compression introduce representation-specific distortions. Since generative compression in many methods treats geometric and color attributes via different parameters, it can induce dimension-specific distortions, motivating multi-dimensional assessment. Moreover, real-world captures generally lack an aligned ground-truth video for a synthesized, continuous camera trajectory, leaving only sparse captured views as references. To enable multi-dimensional quality assessment of 3DGS videos with scarce aligned references, we first present 3DGS-VBench+, a large-scale subjective video quality assessment (VQA) benchmark comprising 3{,}036 3DGS reconstructions, each paired with a rendered video, across 11 real-world and 22 synthetic scenes, generated by 6 representative compression algorithms at systematically designed levels and annotated with 9{,}108 MOSs covering overall, geometry, and color quality. Based on 3DGS-VBench+, we propose 3DGSV-Assessor, a reference-flexible, large multimodal framework that scores all three dimensions in one generation pass and fuses a ranking-based reference cue into the frozen regressor through a bounded gate, supporting both reduced-reference (RR) and no-reference (NR) assessment. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art correlation with human perception on 3DGS-VBench+ and strong zero-shot generalization to other NVS benchmarks. The dataset and code will be released at https://github.com/YukeXing/3DGSV-Assessor.

papers.title: Learning to Falsify: Hierarchical Multiple Instance Learning for High Resolution AI-Generated Image Detection
papers.abstract: Recent advances in generative models have made synthetic images increasingly photorealistic, posing growing challenges to reliable and generalizable detection of AI-generated images. Existing methods typically rely on holistic image-level classification, which may overlook local artifacts, especially in high-resolution images. To address this limitation, we formulate this task as a falsification-driven multiple instance learning problem, where a single fake patch can falsify the whole image, while a real image requires all patches to be authentic. Based on this formulation, we propose \textit{Learning to Falsify (LTF)}, a hierarchical multiple instance learning framework that models an image as multiple bags of instances across different spatial levels and aggregates their predictions under the falsification-inspired principle. We further introduce Cross-Shuffle during training to encourage the model to learn local artifact evidence rather than image-level shortcuts. Furthermore, we propose the \textit{Falsification-driven Test-time Aggregation Strategy (FATAS)}, a plug-and-play module that extends the same falsification-inspired principle to existing detectors by aggregating patch-level predictions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LTF achieves strong generalization and robustness across multiple benchmarks, while FATAS substantially improves representative detectors in high-resolution scenarios without retraining. Code is available at https://github.com/HuiGuanLab/LTF.git

papers.title: Rondo: Controlling Reordering in High-Throughput Packet Spraying
papers.abstract: Modern datacenter applications demand high network bandwidth, motivating packet-level multipath transport to exploit the aggregate capacity of multiple paths. However, packet reordering under packet spraying poses challenges for hardware transports. Excessive packet reordering makes it difficult to infer packet loss, imposes substantial pressure on NIC resources, and ultimately degrades performance. Existing transports either prioritize throughput without controlling packet reordering, or mitigate reordering by restricting transmissions, which leaves available path capacity unused. In this paper, we identify two fundamental sources of packet reordering: transient inter-path queueing differences caused by control dynamics, and persistent path-delay differences due to path heterogeneity. These observations motivate a joint design of a multipath controller and a packet scheduler to address transient and persistent delay differences, respectively. We present Rondo, a packet-level multipath transport that achieves both high throughput and low packet reordering. Its multipath controller uses ACK-based per-path capacity estimation and probing to maintain stable path loads, while its packet scheduler adjusts packet transmission order to compensate for persistent delay differences. Testbed experiments and large-scale simulations show that Rondo reduces the maximum out-of-order degree by up to 97.5% while maintaining high throughput. With constrained receiver buffers, Rondo achieves up to 8.51 times higher goodput.

papers.title: Deep Plug-and-Play Proximal Distance Algorithm for Robust Principal Component Analysis
papers.abstract: Robust Principal Component Analysis (RPCA) is essential in signal processing, with applications in hyperspectral imaging, face recognition, and video background modeling. Traditional RPCA methods often suffer from insufficient utilization of data priors and struggle to capture complex image structures. Conversely, advanced deep denoisers like DnCNN, FFDNet, and DRUNet excel at leveraging image data priors but lack physical model constraints and demonstrate poor robustness against structured noise in RPCA tasks. This paper proposes a novel Plug-and-Play (PnP) method for multi-channel RPCA, integrating both the physical generative model and cutting-edge deep priors. Extensive experiments on RGB and hyperspectral datasets show that PnP-PDA achieves better quantitative performance than conventional RPCA methods and state-of-the-art methods, including deep denoisers and tensor RPCA approaches, while preserving visual details.

papers.title: Isolated symplectic singularities admitting symplectic resolutions
papers.abstract: We give a proof that an isolated algebraic symplectic singularity of dimension $2n\ge 4$ admitting a projective symplectic resolution is analytically isomorphic to the minimal nilpotent orbit closure in $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}$ at the origin.

papers.title: CardioVascBench:Prioritized Diagnosis Generation from Real-World Chinese Cardiovascular Records
papers.abstract: Identifying the primary diagnosis alone does not fully characterize a model's diagnosis-generation performance. We introduce CardioVascBench, a retrospective benchmark for prioritized diagnosis generation from real-world Chinese cardiovascular inpatient records. It contains 3,262 de-identified cases, with 2,174 for training and 1,088 for evaluation, linking clinical narratives and textual ECG reports to expert-verified, ordered discharge diagnoses standardized to ICD-10. An English translation of the evaluation set supports aligned cross-lingual comparison. Our evaluation protocol combines terminology normalization and rank-aware scoring to separately assess primary-diagnosis identification, reference-diagnosis coverage, and list precision. Evaluation across 36 systems shows that higher primary-diagnosis accuracy does not necessarily imply higher list precision against discharge references. We also provide CardioKG-Agent, a knowledge-enhanced baseline combining entity normalization, constrained graph retrieval, and guideline evidence. In a staged comparison of three baseline models, supervised fine-tuning plus the agent achieves a 73.5% higher mean composite score than fine-tuning alone, representing a system-level gain. These results measure retrospective agreement with recorded diagnoses; agreement between metric rankings and physician judgments remains to be validated. CardioVascBench supports research on diagnosis prioritization and knowledge-enhanced generation.

authors.name: Zhen Song
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

papers.title: Think Less, Locally: Local Preference Learning for Reasoning Compression
papers.abstract: Large reasoning models achieve strong performance on challenging tasks, but their long chain-of-thought often incurs substantial inference costs by continuing to deliberate after sufficient information has been obtained. Existing reasoning compression methods primarily operate on reasoning trajectories, paying less attention to the local decision of whether further reasoning is necessary given the current state. We propose LoCo, a local preference learning method for reasoning compression. LoCo detects candidate overthinking states from the model's own traces, freezes the corresponding reasoning prefixes, regenerates shorter verified continuations from the same states, and trains on the resulting state-conditioned preference pairs with DPO. This formulation teaches the model when to continue reasoning and when to conclude, rather than simply encouraging shorter trajectories overall. We construct training data entirely from self-generated mathematical traces and evaluate LoCo on five mathematical and three code generation benchmarks. LoCo reduces completion length by 41.7\%--45.4\% on mathematics and 23.4\%--36.3\% on code, while maintaining or improving accuracy and achieving the best AUC across all code benchmarks. LoCo consistently improves the accuracy-efficiency trade-off on mathematics and transfers effectively to code generation despite math-only training, demonstrating the cross-domain generality of local preference learning for reasoning compression. The code and model will be publicly released at https://github.com/MuyaoYuan/LoCo.

papers.title: Assignment-Free Swarm Navigation via Adaptive Target-Field Planning and Mean-Shift Exploration
papers.abstract: Mean-shift exploration enables assignment-free swarm shape assembly, but obstacle-constrained navigation additionally requires coordinated adaptation of the desired morphology and its physical execution. This paper presents an environment-adaptive navigation framework that integrates target-field planning, execution regulation, and morphology-preserving mean-shift exploration. A feasibility-aware graph search plans the position, orientation, and morphology of an unlabeled target field without specifying robot-specific goals. An execution-regulated reference manager adjusts field progression and morphology switching using swarm entering, coverage, and lag metrics. A moving-frame controller separates prescribed rigid motion from local mean-shift redistribution and incorporates neighbor interactions and obstacle responses. Simulations and hardware experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework coordinates morphology transitions and collective motion for assignment-free swarm navigation through cluttered environments.

papers.title: Feeling of Knowing in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Post-training updates change what large language models (LLMs) can answer, but may leave their answerability judgments misaligned. We study this knowledge-judgment desynchronization through functional feeling of knowing (FoK), which supports selective generation, retrieval triggering, and model routing without implying subjective experience. We propose two trainable channels: a knowledge channel that changes answerability and a FoK channel that judges the current knowledge state. Three stages train them: on-policy supervised fine-tuning (OP-SFT) updates knowledge from corrected on-policy answers; knowledge-delta FoK training (K$\Delta$-FT) adapts judgments across intermediate knowledge states; and FoK-guided policy optimization (FGPO) trains the subsequent answer or explanation. Factual-QA experiments, cross-dataset evaluation, and three sequential updates show that explicit FoK alignment improves judgment quality on updated knowledge. MMLU and ARC-Easy separately assess capability preservation.

papers.title: Deep Neural Operator Learning for stochastic heat equations and applications
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a universal approximation theorem for solution operators of semilinear stochastic heat equations in spatial dimension \(d\ge2\), extending deep neural operator approximation results to SPDEs with distribution-valued Gaussian forcing. A smooth Fourier cutoff reduces the forcing to finitely many measurements, while Besov and Schauder estimates control the resulting solution error. The finite-dimensional solution map is then approximated by ReLU branch networks together with grid-based trunk functions, yielding explicit bounds on the numbers of forcing measurements and trunk functions and approximation in every finite stochastic moment. For linear equations, the reduction coincides with truncation of the first Wiener chaos. Lastly, as an application, we prove a high-probability local-in-time approximation theorem for stochastic Navier--Stokes equations, with finite measurements of both the initial condition and forcing and an explicit sensing rate.

papers.title: The Power of Interaction in Locally Edge-Private Subgraph Counting
papers.abstract:
We study (non-induced) subgraph counting under interactive local edge differential privacy (LEDP). Given a fixed pattern graph $H$ with $k$ vertices, $\ell\ge1$ edges, and $q$ connected components, our goal is to approximately count its copies in an arbitrary $n$-vertex undirected graph while preserving edge privacy.
  We give two complementary accuracy guarantees. First, for every $H$, we give Linear Noise Cancellation (LNC), a two-round $\varepsilon$-LEDP algorithm with additive error and root mean square error both $O(n^{k-3/2}/\varepsilon^\ell)$ on every $n$-vertex graph. For fixed sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, this improves the optimal noninteractive additive error for triangles by a factor of $\sqrt n$ and gives the same improvement in worst-case root mean square error for all cliques on at least three vertices. To our knowledge, this is the first separation between interactive and noninteractive LEDP subgraph counting, showing that a single additional round can improve worst-case accuracy polynomially.
  Second, we determine how accuracy improves when the graph has maximum degree at most a public bound $d$. Our Predict and Correct (PC) framework gives an $(\ell+2)$-round $\varepsilon$-LEDP algorithm with additive error $O(n^{q-1/2}d^{k-q-1}\log^{3\ell-2}n/\varepsilon^\ell)$. For connected patterns, its polynomial factor is $\sqrt n\,d^{k-2}$, giving sublinear error on constant-degree graphs at fixed privacy. We prove matching lower bounds in $n$ and $d$, up to logarithmic factors at fixed privacy, even under arbitrary interaction and approximate privacy with sufficiently small $\delta$. At $d=\Theta(n)$, the lower bound also establishes the optimality of LNC's dependence on $n$.

authors.institution: Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development

papers.title: M\"obius: A Unified Motion-Language Model Bridging Understanding and Generation
papers.abstract: We aim to build a truly unified motion model that can understand, generate, and edit human motion within a single framework. Existing motion UMMs remain only partially unified: motion understanding is handled by a language model, while generation is often delegated to a separate diffusion module operating over learned motion latents. We introduce M\"obius, which brings the entire diffusion process into the same multimodal representation space used for motion understanding. Clean motion, noisy motion, and text jointly participate in shared attention, while role-specific parameters process understanding and generation streams. Importantly, M\"obius operates directly on continuous frame-level raw motion, requiring neither discrete tokenization nor a pretrained motion VAE. This simple formulation naturally supports motion captioning, text-to-motion generation, temporal completion, and instruction-guided editing within a single model. On HumanML3D, M\"obius achieves state-of-the-art performance among unified motion models. Scaling to 1.7B parameters and 1,700 hours of motion data further demonstrates that our framework is both effective and scalable.

papers.title: Weighted Randomized Kaczmarz for Sparsely Corrupted Linear Systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a generalized weighted randomized Kaczmarz framework to approximate solutions to overdetermined linear systems whose measurements are perturbed by sparse, additive corruptions. The proposed framework samples equations with probabilities proportional to a user-defined weighting function of their corresponding residual magnitudes. Our work focuses on weighting functions that will reduce the influence of potentially corrupted equations, and provides analyses for a general class of non-increasing weighting functions. We derive one-step expected squared error bounds that separate progress on uncorrupted equations from the contribution of corrupted equations, and provide sufficient conditions for geometric convergence under one specific family of weighting functions -- threshold weighting. We also investigate adaptive exponential weights scaled by the median or median absolute deviation of residual magnitudes, requiring no prior knowledge of the corruption fraction or magnitudes. Lastly, we consider a family of inverse residual weighting functions. Numerical experiments demonstrate the benefit of such a generalized framework in its flexibility in developing approaches for settings in which information about the corruptions is known or unknown.

papers.title: ZEMA: confidence-calibrated signed descent with only one state
papers.abstract: Recent work characterizes the Adam optimizer as sign descent modulated by gradient uncertainty: the update is the sign of the batch gradient, scaled by how strongly the batch supports that sign. We apply this view directly and introduce ZEMA (Z-score Evidence Momentum Adaptation), which measures that support with a per-coordinate $z$-score computed from the per-example gradients in the current batch, converts it into a sign probability, and smooths the resulting update with a single exponential moving average. Because the probability is formed before smoothing rather than after, ZEMA keeps one state per parameter instead of Adam's two, at a $4.6$ increase in per-step time; the per-example variance it requires can also be estimated from a small fraction of the batch. In fine-tuning and pretraining experiments, ZEMA is competitive with Adam, reduces the variability of the validation loss, and in some settings recovers the sign of the full-dataset gradient more consistently. We close with two directions this opens: extending confidence adaptation beyond the sign geometry, to methods such as Muon, and to differentially private training.

papers.title: The Iterated Local Transitivity Model for oriented graphs
papers.abstract:
Transitivity in social and other complex networks describes the tendency for two nodes with a common neighbor to become adjacent. We propose a new model for complex networks based on transitivity, called the Iterated Local Transitivity Model for Oriented Graphs (ILTO). The model generalizes the Iterated Local Model for Tournaments (ILMT). As in ILMT, oriented graphs are generated iteratively by cloning nodes and their adjacencies, with arcs between clones oriented either as the corresponding arcs between their parents or in the reverse direction. This process produces dense oriented graphs and, under suitable conditions, graphs with high connectivity and small diameter.
  We analyze the universality properties of ILTO, showing that, for generating sequences with infinite support, the base oriented graph determines which oriented graphs appear as induced subgraphs, unlike in ILMT. We study motifs in ILTO and show that when the base graph is a tournament and the generating sequence has infinite support, the model generates quasirandom tournament sequences. Finally, we study domination numbers, the cop number, and the dichromatic number. We bound the cop number in terms of the independence number of the base graph and show that, for each fixed base graph, the dichromatic number is $\Theta(2^t)$ after $2t$ consecutive 0-steps.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Functional Tucker Method with RKHS Factors for Sparse Spatiotemporal Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Reconstructing physical dynamics from fixed sparse sensors and missing frames is a fundamental challenge in scientific research. Sparsity leaves large regions of the field unconstrained, making the inverse problem ill-posed: a model may fit the observed sensors while producing inaccurate off-sensor structures or unreliable predictions between support frames. To this end, we propose PhysFTM---a physics-informed functional Tucker model that parameterizes the Tucker mode factors in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHSs) and incorporates PDE constraints through finite-difference residuals evaluated at off-sensor collocation points. These residuals provide additional physical information in regions without direct observational supervision. PhysFTM first reconstructs continuous spatial fields at support frames via an alternating minimization scheme, optimizing the Tucker core tensor and the RKHS-based factors separately. To enable missing-frame reconstruction, PhysFTM constructs a continuous trajectory in Tucker-core space, which is decoded by the learned spatial RKHS-FTM representation to recover the full spatiotemporal field. Experiments on Allen--Cahn, Navier--Stokes, three-dimensional Heat equations, and a three-dimensional gridded Copernicus ocean reanalysis demonstrate accurate 2D/3D reconstruction under two missing-frame protocols. Code is available at https://github.com/liusirzzz/PhysFTM.

papers.title: The smallest-parts function and elliptic curves
papers.abstract: Recently, Ono established a new connection between partition congruences and the arithmetic of elliptic curves by expressing the partition function $p(n)$ as a CM trace on the modular curve $X_0(6)$. This approach yields new proofs of Ramanujan-type congruences for the partition function modulo powers of $5$, $7$, and $11$, revealing how the geometry of supersingular elliptic curves and the arithmetic of oriented optimal embeddings govern these congruence properties. Motivated by Ono's work, we develop an analogous passage from CM traces to congruences modulo $5$, $7$, and $13$ for the for Andrews's smallest-parts partition function $spt(n)$, employing the established theta-lift and modular-trace methods suited to this setting. With $P$ the Bruinier--Ono weight-zero weak Maass function and $f$ an explicit weakly holomorphic modular function on $\Gamma_0(6)$, the Ahlgren--Andersen formula expresses $spt(n)$ as one twelfth of the discriminant $1-24n$ CM trace of $f-P$. We explain the theta-lift normalization, the contribution of the two orientations, and the harmonic-Maass-form uniqueness argument. Following Garvan's work, we construct integral forms $G_\ell$ of weight $\ell+1$ on $\Gamma_0(\ell)$, compute their Fricke transformations, and prove the exact identities $$ \mathcal T_5(G_5)=-5E_6,\qquad \mathcal T_7(G_7)=-7E_8,\qquad \mathcal T_{13}(G_{13})=13E_{14}. $$ Their reductions yield the three congruences on the Andrews's smallest-parts partition function. We also give a supersingular specialization of the trace of $f$, with actual reduction multiplicities, and explain the role of imprimitive forms, the conductor restriction in CM reduction, and the distinction between the primes $11$ and $13$. These results have been verified in Lean using AxiomProver.

papers.title: Finding Hypercliques Faster Than Brute Force
papers.abstract:
We show that for any fixed $k$, there exists $\varepsilon_k > 0$ such that, given a $(k-1)$-uniform hypergraph $H$ on $n$ vertices, one can count the number of $k$-hypercliques in $H$ in $O(n^{k-\varepsilon_k})$ time. This refutes the hyperclique conjecture of Lincoln, Vassilevska Williams, and Williams (SODA 2018). Our result follows from the uniform construction of a family of arithmetic circuits of size $O(n^{k-\varepsilon_k})$ for the $k$-hyperclique tensor, a natural higher-order generalization of the matrix multiplication tensor.
  We obtain two corollaries. First, for every $k$, there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that Max-$k$SAT can be solved in $2^{(1-\varepsilon)n} \cdot \mathrm{poly}(m,n)$ time. Second, for every $k$, there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that arithmetic progressions of length $k$ in subsets of $\{0,1,\ldots,n\}$ can be detected in $n^{2-\varepsilon}$ time. Both corollaries refute other prominent conjectures in the literature.

authors.name: Ryan Williams
authors.institution: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory

papers.title: Bilateral Protection for Private LoRA Inference with Intel TDX
papers.abstract: Cloud services using private low-rank adaptation (LoRA) must protect client inputs and outputs alongside owners' proprietary parameters and execute the approved adaptation. We design and implement a system for bilateral protection of private LoRA inference using Intel Trust Domain Extensions (TDX), connecting approved application identity to actual artifact consumption and adapter activation. The client and LoRA owner independently verify remote attestation, application identity, and binding to the actual Transport Layer Security (TLS) public key before releasing inputs and the weight-decryption key. A fixed read-only image and verified-byte consumption connect approved identities to inference objects, with all inference inside a trust domain. Experiments on real TDX hardware reject controlled application and boot-parameter modifications before secret release. Across 400 fixed dialogues, protected and native CPU inference in the same trust domain produce identical token sequences for all 400 pairs. Across 12 independent trust-domain boots, the steady-state service-to-native time ratio is 1.0094, with a 95% interval of [1.0064, 1.0126]. The system connects bilateral secret release, approved model use, and task-capability preservation, providing verifiable implementation and cost evidence for confidential inference with a public base and private adapter.

authors.name: Dongbo Yan
authors.institution: Tumor Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University

papers.title: Beyond Local Refinement: Wide-Area Precise Cross-View Localization
papers.abstract: Fine-grained cross-view localization aims to precisely localize a ground camera against geo-referenced aerial imagery, but current methods typically assume a narrow geographic prior, substantially limiting their applicability when upstream localization remains coarse. To bridge this gap, we study this task over much larger aerial regions. However, this seemingly simple extension fundamentally changes the localization problem: the growing disparity in spatial extent between ground and aerial views makes reliable cross-view matching difficult to establish directly, while the increasing number of look-alike locations in larger regions introduces substantial visual ambiguity. To address these challenges, we propose RingMatch, a search-and-verification framework for wide-area cross-view localization. RingMatch first leverages predictive uncertainty to uncover plausible locations and progressively zooms into their surroundings to obtain increasingly fine-grained evidence, yielding a compact set of promising candidates. We then introduce the depth ring, a novel geometric representation that reveals subtle variations in the spatial layout around a location and serves as a view-shared spatial signature for an LVLM verifier to resolve residual ambiguity. To benchmark this setting, we construct VIGOR-Pro by composing VIGOR aerial tiles into contiguous regions with spatial extents of up to 400 m. Experiments show that RingMatch maintains strong localization performance as the aerial region expands, consistently outperforming representative end-to-end and retrieval-based methods.

authors.name: Qi Shi
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University

authors.name: Zonghao Guo
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: GSCV++: Lightweight 3D Gaussian Splatting Sequence Compression via Standard Video Codecs
papers.abstract: This paper presents GSCV++, a lightweight pipeline for 3D {G}aussian {S}platting (GS) sequences {C}ompression with standard {V}ideo codecs. To meet the requirements of low-complexity and hardware compatibility from the industry, GSCV++ jointly improves preprocessing, 3D-to-2D mapping, and practical video compression configuration of GS compression. First, for preprocessing, energy-adaptive inter-frame spherical harmonic (SH) alternative current (AC) dimensionality reduction (EA-SHDR) is proposed to produces a compact and stable temporal SH AC feature space. It can reduce the data volume of following mapping and practical compression, as well as less complexity while eliminating redundant information. Second, for 3D-to-2D mapping, prior-based Inter-MiniPLAS (P-MiniPLAS) is designed to generate smooth 2D feature maps through prior-based weighting factor inference and small scale remapping. Compared with vanilla Parallel Linear Assignment Sorting (PLAS) and Morton scan, P-MiniPLAS ensures the generated 2D maps are more suitable for the video codec while maintaining a low level of computational complexity. Third, for practical compression, content-aware generalized compression (CA-GC) is developed to use a non-uniform bit-depth split for coordinate map generation, and a coding unit size selection is introduced for efficient compression complexity control, which fully exploits the performance of video codecs without involving normative changes. Experiments demonstrate that GSCV++ reports over 20\% in intra- and 60\% in inter-prediction rate-distortion gains compared with state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. GSCV++ also achieves faster 2D map generation, encoding, and decoding than other SOTA methods using the same type of video codecs. Ablation studies verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed modules and provide insights for subsequent research.

authors.name: Li Zhang
authors.institution: Second Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University

papers.title: Quantifying out-of-distribution data severity with Wasserstein distances: benchmarking large language models for alloy property prediction
papers.abstract: As general-purpose Large Language Models (LLMs), such as Gemini and DeepSeek, exhibit increasingly advanced reasoning capabilities, a critical question arises: how do their property prediction abilities compare to those of domain-specific pretrained materials models? In this study, we evaluate predictions for Ti, steels, high-entropy alloy (HEA) and Al, demonstrating that general-purpose LLMs surprisingly outperform SteelBERT, MatSciBERT, and SciBERT. To further enhance performance, we introduce a hybrid approach that utilizes numerical priors from a prior model, such as CatBoost or SteelBERT, to guide the general LLMs (Deepseek V3.1, Gemini-2.5-Flash). By inputting these initial estimates from a prior model as prompts, the LLM acts as a reasoning corrector, achieving accuracy superior to the prior model and "unguided mode". Furthermore, we investigate the impact of data strategy using a similarity-based metric, revealing that data quality dominates quantity; using merely 5% of high-similarity reference data of training set as input yields performance similar to the results of using 100% of training set. Additionally, the LLMs demonstrate excellent uncertainty calibration, where self-reported "high" confidence strongly correlates with minimal deviation from ground truth. Our findings suggest that synergizing general-purpose LLMs with prior model numerical baselines and high-quality data curation creates a cost-effective and accurate paradigm for materials discovery, reducing the need for expensive domain-specific pretraining.

papers.title: Dynamical Phonon Anharmonicity Drives Charge-Density-Wave Softening and Electronic Quasiparticle Decoherence in Monolayer 1H-NbSe2
papers.abstract: Charge-density-wave (CDW) instabilities in two-dimensional materials are governed by strongly anharmonic soft phonons, whose dynamical behavior remains poorly understood beyond the statically renormalized vibrations. Here, using monolayer 1H-NbSe2, we investigate how frequency-dependent three- and four-phonon interactions reshape phonon spectral functions and influence electronic excitations. We find that three-phonon interactions induce substantial dynamical softening of CDW modes, increasing the estimated transition temperature relative to static self-consistent phonon theory. Four-phonon interactions further promote such dynamical softening and enhance spectral broadening, producing non-Lorentzian lineshapes that challenge the quasiparticle picture. Incorporating dynamically renormalized phonon frequencies and electron-phonon coupling into Fan-Migdal electron self-energy calculations reveals enhanced electronic kinks, satellite features, and momentum-dependent quasiparticle decoherence, driven by the strong momentum dependence of the electron-phonon coupling matrix elements. These findings establish dynamical anharmonicity as a critical link between soft-mode lattice fluctuations and electronic spectral signatures, providing insights into coupled lattice-electron dynamics in two-dimensional quantum materials.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Prototype Learning for Open-Set Test-Time Adaptation
papers.abstract: Open-set test-time adaptation (TTA) aims to adapt source-trained models to unlabeled test streams where covariate-shifted in-distribution (csID) samples and covariate-shifted out-of-distribution (csOOD) samples may coexist. Existing TTA methods are typically designed under a closed-set assumption and therefore lack explicit mechanisms for reliably distinguishing csID from csOOD samples. Consequently, csOOD samples may be mistakenly included in confidence-enhancing adaptation, producing harmful gradients that degrade known-class performance. To address this, we propose Uncertainty-Aware Prototype Learning for Open-Set Test-Time Adaptation (UAPA), a plug-and-play method for reliable open-set adaptation. Specifically, we first introduce Uncertainty-Driven ID/OOD Separation, which combines a classifier-prototype score with a mini-batch-normalized evidence-derived uncertainty score to distinguish csID from csOOD samples. We then propose a Dynamic Prototype Refinement strategy that periodically refines class-specific target prototypes using buffered csID features to progressively follow the estimated class directions. Lastly, we introduce Contrastive Prototype Entropy Adaptation, which applies entropy minimization to csID samples and entropy maximization to csOOD samples, while prototype-level contrastive learning aligns csID features with their corresponding target prototypes and reduces the maximum similarity between csOOD features and known-class prototypes. Empirically, UAPA outperforms the strongest baselines on the CIFAR benchmarks and Tiny-ImageNet-C, improving average OSCR by 2.08 and 1.28 percentage points, respectively.

authors.name: Mingkui Tan
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: A face polynomial invariant for embedded graphs
papers.abstract: We introduce the face polynomial of a ribbon graph, a generating function for face numbers under the ribbon group action. It addresses the face-count case of the Ellis--Monaghan--Moffatt question on twisted duality. We derive deletion--contraction recursions and prove that this polynomial coincides with the vertex polynomial for \(\langle\delta\rangle\), \(\langle\delta\tau\rangle\), and \(\langle\delta,\tau\rangle\). We characterize monomial cases and obtain formulas and recursions for Euler-genus partial-twuality polynomials. For orientable graphs, we show that the partial-dual face polynomial has both parities whenever an edge exists, so the partial-dual Euler-genus polynomial has only even exponents.

papers.title: What Sets the Serving Speed of Looped Language Models? Measurements and Optimizations Graded by Exactness
papers.abstract: Looped language models apply one block of layers many times per token, so a serving engine pays every per-layer overhead once per loop; we measure serving for Ouro and Huginn-0125 in an open-source looped-model engine and grade our optimizations from bitwise-identical changes to those that require an accuracy check. At batch 1, fusing all loop submissions leaves Ouro throughput at 0.99x; the 5689 small kernels per token are the real cost, and fusing them behind rounding fences raises throughput 1.11-1.59x while 1014/1014 requests remain identical. An approximate fusion is no faster and misses a one-point GSM8K rule on 87 questions (61 and 62 correct versus 64), so we do not ship it. Huginn's released defaults avoid dead KV slots, reuse prefix-cache pages, and serve 1.77-3.16x faster than the base engine; Ouro reaches 1.65-2.15x and agent sessions 1.91-3.21x, while Huginn's noise and prefix-reuse changes stay within one point on all 1319 Huginn test questions; Huginn's packed prefill, -0.61 points on the same questions, meets that rule only on its point estimate. Position-keyed noise makes CPU cache reuse exact but still leaves 20 of 128 GPU full hits different, while loop fusion delays prefill admission and a 64-graph cache prevents eager fallbacks. Under prefill-decode disaggregation ExactLoop reaches up to 3.3x the base throughput with peer error handling disabled, and 3.1x in two of three runs with it enabled. Its transfer budget, sized to hold one request's KV in flight, cuts the commit tail from about one second under the earlier budget to 16 ms (base: 2.8 s), removing the polling rounds that the engine's interval would otherwise impose.

authors.name: Jiarui Guo
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Dynamics of Vortex Electrons in a Uniform Magnetic Field Across Nonrelativistic and Relativistic Regimes
papers.abstract: The dynamics of a vortex electron in a transverse uniform magnetic field involves not only the cyclotron motion of the wave packet center but also the evolution of its internal wavefunction structure. To study this process, we develop a quantum framework and investigate the dynamics of vortex electrons in both the nonrelativistic and relativistic regimes. A discrete Bessel-Gaussian initial wave packet is expanded in the basis of Dirac eigenstates to obtain the time-dependent wavefunction and to analyze its spatiotemporal evolution. In the nonrelativistic regime, the results deviate significantly from the rigid point-dipole model, as the intrinsic kinetic orbital angular momentum exhibits dynamics more complex than simple Larmor precession, owing to the nonstationary internal current distribution of the wave packet. In the relativistic regime, the nonlinear dependence of the energy levels on the quantum numbers destroys the equal spacing of the spectrum. Consequently, the relative phases among the eigenstate components of the wave packet evolve nonuniformly, resulting in wave-packet spreading and deformation, accompanied by modified intrinsic orbital angular momentum dynamics. We introduce a dimensionless parameter to quantify this relativistic dephasing, providing an approximate criterion for selecting physical parameters and evolution times to mitigate the resulting wave-packet distortion. These results clarify the limitations of the rigid point-dipole model, highlight the essential role of internal wavefunction structure, and provide theoretical guidance for understanding and manipulating relativistic vortex electrons.

authors.name: Zhigang Bu
authors.institution: Shanghai Institute of Optics and Fine Mechanics

papers.title: The Maximum Second Zagreb Spectral Radius of Trees, Unicyclic Graphs and Bicyclic Graphs
papers.abstract: The second Zagreb matrix of a graph $G$ is $Z(G)=D(G)A(G)D(G)$, where $D(G)$ and $A(G)$ are the degree matrix and the adjacency matrix of $G$. For many degree-based weighted adjacency matrices, the trees, unicyclic graphs and bicyclic graphs with the largest spectral radius have a vertex adjacent to all others, and Mei et al. conjectured this for every such matrix on unicyclic graphs. Jiang et al. showed that $Z(G)$ is a counterexample. We prove that, for $q\in\{0,1,2\}$ and every $n\ge4$, the connected graph of order $n$ and cyclomatic number $q$ maximizing the spectral radius of $Z(G)$ is unique, and is obtained from two adjacent vertices with $q$ common neighbours by attaching $n-q-2$ pendent vertices to them as evenly as possible. The only exceptions are the star for $q=0$ and $n\le7$, and the triangle with one pendent vertex at each vertex for $q=1$ and $n=6$. This confirms a conjecture of Jiang et al.\ and all three parts of a conjecture of Shen and Shan for this matrix, with best possible thresholds on $n$. For $n\ge8$, the maximum value is $\lfloor (n+q)^2/4\rfloor+(n+q)/2+7q-2+O(1/n)$, whereas the star gives only $(n-1)^{3/2}$. A key tool is a determinant criterion that reduces spectral comparisons to sign conditions on explicit polynomials.

papers.title: BhopalMLS: A LiDAR Dataset for Semantic Scene Understanding in Heterogeneous Urban Environments
papers.abstract: We introduce BhopalMLS, a large-scale Mobile Laser Scanning (MLS) dataset from a dense, heterogeneous urban environment in Bhopal, India, with mixed traffic, informal structures, and narrow unplanned streets. It spans approximately 10 km of road corridors with over 1.2 billion points and 19,518 annotated instances across 62 fine-grained static categories, grouped into 12-class and 21-class benchmark taxonomies; 6 optional moving-class subclasses support dynamic-object analysis. Existing 3D datasets, collected in well-planned cities, are structurally more uniform than such unplanned settings, and lack their subtype diversity. On semantic and instance segmentation at both granularities, fine-tuned foundation models surpass supervised baselines: Utonia(L) reaches 71.28% mIoU (vs. PTv3's 68.04% from scratch) and 44.07% mAP50 on the 12-class benchmark. Cross-region experiments against four established datasets (Ke-MLS, Toronto-3D, Paris-Lille-3D, SemanticKITTI) reveal a consistent asymmetric transferability: models trained on BhopalMLS transfer better than the reverse on every pair, for both Utonia(L) and Concerto(L) (mean 21.5, up to 36 mIoU points), holding even when the target is denser. Factor-controlled retraining at a fixed label budget, repeated on both models, attributes this to the coverage of BhopalMLS's subtype inventory rather than to dataset size or corridor geometry: collapsing each class to a single subtype costs 13.0 and 13.3 mIoU points for Utonia(L) and Concerto(L). BhopalMLS therefore offers a testbed for 3D perception beyond well-planned cities. Data and an interactive viewer are at https://geoai4cities.github.io/bhopalmls.

authors.name: Pyare Lal Chauhan
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Bhopal

papers.title: On the Learnability of Footwear Robustness: Footstep Recognition Under Unseen Conditions
papers.abstract: Footstep patterns, captured using pressure or force-sensitive walkways during natural walking, offer a convenient and passive approach to biometric recognition. However, footwear variability poses a major challenge to practical deployment, as it impacts both the foot-sensor interface and the user's underlying gait mechanics. This study considers the particularly difficult scenario where users enroll under one fixed footwear condition but must later be recognized in arbitrary, unseen footwear. Using the StepUP-P150 dataset, we show that footwear-induced shift, while substantial and heterogeneous across individuals, contains shared structure that can be learned from a training population and transferred, zero-shot, to previously unseen users and footwear styles. We do this using BiStepNet, a novel architecture that decomposes spatial and temporal identity cues into independently trainable streams and outperforms compact 3D spatiotemporal baselines for cross-footwear recognition. We demonstrate that cross-footwear recognition performance scales systematically with the volume and diversity of footwear representation in the training set, with gains transferring to footwear styles not directly observed during training. Moreover, we show that auxiliary gait datasets with only partial modality overlap (incorporated through the architecture's decomposed design) can be leveraged to further improve robustness to unseen footwear conditions.

papers.title: Mixture of Wide Experts: Sparse Routing for Interpretable Native Coordinates
papers.abstract:
Language models often spread a concept across many internal dimensions, making their features difficult to interpret. Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) recover clearer features after training. We ask whether models can instead learn interpretable output coordinates directly. We introduce Mixture of Wide Experts (MoWE), a sparse feed-forward layer in which selected experts read the full representation but write to fixed, disjoint output coordinates. On a controlled task with known hidden causes, this design preserves predictive performance while localizing causes more clearly than dense and standard mixture-of-experts (MoE) models.
  At approximately matched compute, we train two 19-layer runs of each architecture for 10 billion tokens. MoWE achieves evaluation cross-entropy 2.417 versus 2.452 for dense, while standard MoE reaches 2.22.
  We measure native-coordinate readability by asking a language-model judge to describe each coordinate from passages where it is strongly active and test that description on new passages. Correcting for descriptions that also fit other coordinates gives a specificity score of 0.523 for MoWE, 0.375 for dense, and 0.268 for standard MoE. TopK SAEs trained on the same FFN updates score 0.489 for dense and 0.556 for MoWE, making native MoWE comparable to the dense SAE.
  In the first case study, we identify a four-coordinate causal path supporting the model's prediction of degrees after the prompt A right angle is 90. We then copy seven angle-related coordinate values into the model as it processes A rectangle has four, changing its next-token prediction from sides to degrees. In the second, one fixed coordinate set detects hazardous requests and another steers the next token toward refusal. These examples show that MoWE combines sparse conditional computation with coordinates that can be identified and reused directly.

papers.title: Solar extreme-ultraviolet waves and other associated solar activities
papers.abstract: Extreme ultraviolet (EUV) waves are large-scale, tsunami like disturbances on the solar surface associated with eruptive phenomena such as solar flares, filament eruptions, and coronal mass ejections (CMEs). Because their strong correlation with major solar eruptions, we present here a comprehensive statistical study of EUV waves and their connections to Moreton waves, CMEs, solar flares, type II radio bursts, and solar energetic particle (SEP) events during Solar Cycle 25 (December 2019-December 2025). This study utilizes EUV data from the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly onboard the Solar Dynamics Observatory and coronagraph data from the Large Angle and Spectrometric Coronagraph onboard Solar and Heliospheric Observatory. Our analysis reveals that 12.3% of the observed EUV waves are associated with Moreton waves, 95% with CMEs, 92.7% associated with flares, 44.3% with metric type II radio bursts, and 11.8% with SEPs. While nearly all EUV waves are linked to CMEs, their association with solar flares varies significantly, ranging from weak B-class events to major X-class flares. Furthermore, the majority of Moreton waves correlate with large- or medium-class flares, with only a small fraction associated with weaker C-class flares. Our findings may contribute to a better understanding of space weather events and, potentially, to their forecasting.

papers.title: Variance-Reduced Stochastic Quasi-Newton SQCQP Method for Nonlinear Programming Problems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a variance-reduced stochastic quasi-Newton sequential quadratic constrained quadratic programming method (VR-QN-SQCQP) for finite-sum nonlinear optimization with equality and inequality constraints. Exact nonlinear-constraint Hessians are replaced entirely by safeguarded symmetric rank-one (SR1) curvature models built from first-order constraint gradients, while PAGE estimates the objective gradient and an exact \(L_1\) merit function provides globalization. Under explicit regularity, boundedness, relative QCQP-accuracy, and step-length assumptions, the analysis establishes almost-sure subsequential convergence to Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) points and, under stronger uniform step-length and error-control conditions, an expected \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) outer-iteration bound for the squared KKT residual. A conditional local stability result also compares learned-curvature directions with their exact-Hessian counterparts. Numerical experiments compare VR-QN-SQCQP against Exact-SQCQP-PAGE on Sparse PCA using 253,680 CDC BRFSS 2015 observations and on a dense nonlinear benchmark. Over ten seeds, both methods converge in all Sparse PCA runs, while on the dense benchmark the proposed method converges in 10/10 runs versus 9/10 for the exact-Hessian variant. The proposed method performs zero exact constraint-Hessian evaluations and reduces median curvature-construction time on the dense benchmark from 0.1230 s to 0.0111 s. Overall runtime benefits remain problem-dependent.

authors.name: Gopal Tiwari
authors.institution: ICAR-National Bureau of Soil Survey and Land Use Planning

papers.title: Exact Rokhsar-Kivelson points hosting first-order phase transitions in $S=1$ compass models
papers.abstract: We study $S=1$ compass models on the square and kagome lattices with bond-dependent bilinear and biquadratic interactions parametrized by an angle $\theta$. For compatible geometries, we determine the exact ground-state manifolds throughout the interval $\pi/4\leq\theta\leq3\pi/4$. At each endpoint, a product of on-site unitaries maps the Hamiltonian to the Laplacian of a configuration graph $\mathcal{G}$ in the $S=1$ Cartesian basis. These endpoints are exact Rokhsar-Kivelson (RK) points, with one ground state per dynamically connected component of $\mathcal{G}$. Each such state is an equal-amplitude superposition in the transformed basis and acquires configuration-dependent phases upon transforming back to the original basis. Both models possess $m=O(L)$ independent and mutually commuting conserved $\mathbb{Z}_2$ line charges, where $L$ is the linear system size, forcing a ground-state degeneracy of at least $2^m$ at the RK endpoints. Throughout the interior region, $\pi/4<\theta<3\pi/4$, the ground-state manifold on each lattice is instead spanned by two product states, both annihilated by the Hamiltonian. On both lattices, each RK endpoint also hosts a first-order transition into this intervening interior phase spanned by the two product states with long-range order.

authors.name: Jay Pandey
authors.institution: Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani

papers.title: PACT: Pose-Robust Actuation Co-Design for Tendon-Driven Robotic Hands
papers.abstract: Humanoid robotic hands must provide sufficient force, speed, and backdrivability within a human-scale envelope. Tendon-driven transmissions address this challenge by relocating actuators to the palm and forearm, but routing paths, moment arms, and capstan dimensions jointly determine both force capability and joint speed, so selecting them sequentially satisfies one requirement at the expense of the other. This paper presents a pose-robust actuation co-design for tendon-driven robot hands (PACT) framework that optimizes tendon routing, moment arms, and capstan dimensions under pose-dependent force requirements and drivetrain-bandwidth constraints. A feasible-force formulation enforces actuator bounds and equilibrium at all joints, while a max-min objective maximizes task-force coverage at the weakest pose. Applied to a four-degree-of-freedom finger, the framework produces an asymmetric N + 1 tendon topology using quasi-direct-drive actuators. Across eight poses, the design achieves task-force coverage of 0.88-1.00 and a predicted 5 Hz minimum isolated-joint flexion/extension bandwidth within a 70th-percentile human-size envelope. Prototype measurements deviate from predictions by up to 24.5%, primarily due to unmodeled transmission losses. These results indicate that co-designing routing with the drivetrain can meet pose-dependent force requirements without relaxing the bandwidth constraint, paving the way for human-sized robotic hands with human-level performance.

papers.title: FloMo: 3D Scene Flow as a World Action Model Intermediate for Learning from Human Video
papers.abstract: Pretrained video generation models distill internet-scale motion priors into robot policies, but full video is a redundant signal for action prediction. We argue that dense 3D motion is the medium through which video pretraining best transfers to robot actions, and that predicting motion rather than video affords better sample-efficiency for action prediction. FloMo is a 5B video-generation model fine-tuned to predict 3D scene-flow and action tokens. Rendering scene flow as RGB and encoding it into the same latent space as video enables a pretrained video generation backbone to efficiently adapt to predict 3D scene flow. Co-trained on action-free human video and action-labeled robot teleoperation data, our model benefits from human-video pretraining and generalizes to unseen objects, motion primitives, and tasks. Replacing motion prediction with a video prediction objective degrades out-of-distribution generalization, while adding a video prediction target alongside motion lowers policy success rather than improving it. When motion, video, and action are predicted jointly, action tokens attend far more to motion than to video, suggesting that predicting video wastes model capacity. Together, these results indicate that motion effectively mediates the transfer from video pretraining to action. More information can be found at flomo-wam.github.io.

authors.name: Ayush Agarwal
authors.institution: All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Rajkot

papers.title: When Cell Crops Share a Parent: Measuring and Isolating Acquisition Leakage in Cervical Cytology Benchmarks
papers.abstract: Public cervical cytology benchmarks release many cell crops cut from far fewer microscope fields or slides and are often split at the crop level, so test cells share acquisition parents with training cells. In a preregistered study, crop-level splitting raised SIPaKMeD accuracy by 0.97 percentage points across twelve architectures and twenty seeds (95% CI 0.59-1.39), and CRIC accuracy by 12.08 points (11.16-12.99). On SIPaKMeD, a factorial that fixes training crop and parent counts attributes the gain to sibling exposure (1.73 points, 0.95-2.51), not to the extra parent diversity of crop-level splits (0.00). Parent identity is decodable at about 100 times chance, yet erasing 82% of its above-floor linear recoverability left the gap unchanged, and Grad-CAM did not distinguish leaking from clean models; matching test cells' color statistics to an unseen same-class field removed most of the advantage. Decodability and saliency cannot substitute for a parent-disjoint split.

papers.title: A Resonant-Tunneling Quantum-Dot Demultiplexer for Scalable Cryogenic Single-Electron Routing
papers.abstract: Scaling quantum electronic systems such as quantum-dot spin qubits and single-electron devices is increasingly limited by the wiring overhead between cryogenic devices and room-temperature control electronics. Multi-channel quantum-dot architectures that selectively route electrons using a few shared control lines, analogous to demultiplexers in classical networks, offer a promising solution. Here, we propose and theoretically investigate a gate-defined architecture of three parallel quantum dots sharing a common source reservoir and coupled to independent drain channels. Using an analytical electrostatic model and tight-binding quantum transport simulations, we show that the device can act as an on-chip single-electron demultiplexer based on resonant tunneling in the cryogenic regime. Closed-system eigenstate analysis reveals localized orbital states in each dot, and open-system transport calculations show resonant conductance peaks when these levels align with the incident electron energy, consistent with the closed-system eigenenergy evolution. By engineering the barrier-gate spacing and the relative plunger-gate dimensions, we obtain well-separated resonances with minimal overlap between channels. Bond-current density calculations show that transport is confined to the resonant channel with negligible leakage into neighboring outputs, yielding channel selectivity approaching unity for all resonant modes. The architecture is compatible with Si/SiGe and GaAs/AlGaAs platforms and can be extended to more channels, offering a route toward programmable quantum routing and resonant-tunneling-based quantum circuitry.

authors.name: Rajat Bharadwaj
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Thiruvananthapuram

authors.name: Madhu Thalakulam
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Thiruvananthapuram

papers.title: Alignment Faking Depends on the Value, Not Just the Model
papers.abstract: Language models can follow a directive when they believe they are monitored and abandon it when they believe they are not, a pattern termed Alignment Faking. Prior work establishes this for harmful-content objectives and a handful of moral-foundations values, leaving open how it distributes across a wider value space. We argue it is value-dependent: whether compliance survives a change in perceived oversight is a property of the model--value pairing, not of the model alone. Our framework profiles Alignment Faking per value, scoring each model-value pair under three conditions: bare (no system prompt), unmonitored, and monitored. On 32 ValueBench dimensions across ten open- and closed-weight models (8B-~675B), compliance gaps span 0.05-0.50, with a distilled 70B above a ~675B model. We observe that majority of the structural variance depends on which model was asked about which value and not on the model or value alone. A six-category taxonomy over reasoning traces tracks the behavioural shift: training-signal reasoning dominates under monitoring and value-conflict reasoning dominates when unmonitored. We package per-model results as value cards, extending model cards with behavioral disposition. Code and data are available at https://github.com/respailab/VALET.

papers.title: Bicarbonate/carbonic acid equilibria in aqueous solutions: Conformational Dynamics, Ion-Pair Speciation, and Free Energy Landscapes from Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics and Metadynamics
papers.abstract: Carbonic acid (H2CO3) is connected with the dissolved CO2 and bicarbonate (HCO3-) equilibria in aqueous solutions. Its two elementary reactions in water, acid dissociation and dehydration to CO2, are difficult to resolve because both are coupled to proton transfer through hydrogen-bonded networks. In this work, we combine 0.5 ns of unbiased PBE-D3 molecular dynamics of 1 molar solution of H2CO3 with metadynamics on the O - H coordination (H2CO3 = HCO3- + H+) and the C - O distance of the leaving hydroxyl (H2CO3 <=> CO2 + H2O). These unbiased trajectories show frequent cis-cis <=> cis-trans interconversion through long-lived bicarbonate (well separated from solvated proton, H3O+, and also mediated by a short-lived three-water [H2O...H3O+...H2O] ring that acts as a solvent-shared ion pair (SSIP); only 16-23% of deprotonation events reach a solvent-separated ion pair (SShIP). Resolving ion-pairs as SSIP for proper reaction leads to an improved estimate of pKa1 from 1.1 to 2.4, toward the experimental 3.45-3.59 (measured at supposedly infinite dilution). Further, metadynamics simulations provide a dehydration barrier of 17.8 (1D) and 15.3 kcal/mol (2D), suggesting that the final product CO2 + H2O is 2.8 kcal/mol below H2CO3. Our two-dimensional free energy surface also shows that C--O cleavage proceeds through the CO2 + OH- which further goes down by 9.9 kcal/mol to product CO2 + H2O.

papers.title: JevBreak: Your Model, Their Decision
papers.abstract: Restricting what a model can say is often mistaken for restricting an attacker's influence over its decision. An attacker can add text to the evidence and steer the model toward a wrong answer that still belongs to the allowed set. We evaluate seven decision models spanning hosted APIs, open-weight models and an encoder on 16 tasks in seven domains from Decision Bench, targeting every wrong option across 240 text examples (990 targets per model). We present Slot Attack, a black-box attack designed for decision models that appends text assembled from named components to steer predictions toward an attacker-selected incorrect option. The method relies solely on returned label probabilities, achieves success rates of 32--99\% on initially correct decisions, and identifies the effective component combinations with a median of 17--72 queries per successful attack. Accuracy and confidence do not reliably reveal this vulnerability. Models with near-identical accuracy on the sampled tasks differ by about 20\%age points in attack success. We demonstrate that an attacker can force not just one wrong answer but every available one: on about 20\% of correct decisions for the JEV models, 77\% for gpt-6-luna and 98\% for GLiNER2.5; a confidence threshold does not reliably screen the attack out. A fixed answer set constrains a decision's form, not its source; robustness must be measured per model, per task and per version rather than assumed from output format.

papers.title: Constructions of Variable Modified Chaplygin-Jacobi and Chaplygin-Abel Gases from Geometrothermodynamics
papers.abstract: Understanding the physical origin of the Universe's late-time accelerated expansion remains one of the central open problems in modern cosmology. Geometrothermodynamics (GTD) offers a compelling route to this problem, providing a geometric framework that unifies thermodynamics with contact and Riemannian geometry to encode the equilibrium properties of a physical system directly into its underlying geometric structure. In this work, we employ the GTD formalism to investigate cosmological models capable of explaining the observed accelerated expansion of the Universe. As an important outcome, our simple model exhibits dynamical behavior that provides a reasonable description of the late-time evolution of the Universe. We study the Chaplygin-Jacobi and Chaplygin-Abel gas models and their variable forms within geometrothermodynamics by deriving their thermodynamic relations, entropy, and equations of state. The free parameters of the models are constrained through a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis using several observational datasets, including cosmic chronometers combined with baryon acoustic oscillations (CC+BAO), DESI DR2 BAO data, DESI DR2 combined with the DES-SN5YR and Union3 Type Ia supernova compilations. The statistical performance of the models is assessed using the Akaike and Bayesian Information Criteria (AIC and BIC). We further examine their cosmological evolution through the deceleration parameter, the dark-energy equation-of-state parameter, and higher-order kinematic diagnostics, including the jerk and snap parameters. The perturbative stability of the models is also investigated through the squared sound speed.

authors.institution: Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology, Shibpur

papers.title: Stress-Testing the Robustness of LLM-Based Causal Inference
papers.abstract: Why do some of the world's most powerful Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems still struggle to reason about cause and effect? Causal discovery, the ability to discern the underlying drivers of a system, is fundamental to scientific inquiry and has traditionally relied on structured data and statistical methods. Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have been explored as an alternative paradigm for causal inference, leveraging their broad knowledge and reasoning capabilities. Yet, despite their linguistic fluency, LLMs often rely on surface-level pattern recognition rather than genuine causal logic. While it is known that LLMs stumble in this domain, we lack a precise map of where, why, and how significantly these failures occur. In this paper, we propose a systematic stress-test framework across six critical dimensions: model scale, causal graph complexity, prompting strategy, metadata quality, data quality, and sensitivity to uncertainty. Our findings reveal a significant "optimism bias" in LLMs; models consistently overestimate causal links, leading to low precision across the board. Furthermore, we demonstrate that traditional evaluation metrics can be deceptive: while reasoning-heavy models lead in performance, the highest scores often occur when uncertainty in inference is overlooked. Once uncertainty is integrated into the evaluation, performance drops, providing a more honest reflection of causal reliability. We also find that, while scaling model size improves outcomes, these gains are fragile; performance degrades sharply as the quality of metadata decreases. This work serves as a practical guide to the blind spots of LLMs, offering a clear-eyed assessment of when these tools can be integrated into a causal discovery pipeline and when they are likely to lead researchers astray.

authors.name: Jigarkumar Patel
authors.institution: Sardar Vallabhbhai National Institute of Technology Surat

papers.title: Twice as Fast, Until It Isn't: Quantized Serving of Mid-Size Open LLMs
papers.abstract: A team serving a 9B-20B open-weight language model on vLLM or SGLang must choose a quantization recipe, and needs two numbers: the speedup over BF16 and the accuracy given up. We assemble every public measurement of these numbers that we could verify and find that the record supplies them only in pieces. Only two checkpoints, both INT4 builds of Gemma 3 12B, have both a vLLM timing and an accuracy score, and that score covers a single MMLU subject, one that the AWQ build was calibrated on. The batch-1 timings predate current engine releases, AMD and Intel Gaudi have no timing in this band at all, and FP4 has none against BF16. The timings that do exist follow one rule. Decoding a small batch is limited by memory bandwidth, so 4-bit weights roughly double speed (2.12x for Qwen2.5-14B on an A100), but the gain vanishes once a large batch makes the GPU compute-bound (1.02x for Gemma 3 12B at batch size 256), where FP8 is the recipe that can still help. Many published accuracy deltas, including every HumanEval delta, lie within benchmark sampling noise. We close with a seven-item reporting checklist for future measurements.

authors.name: Smit Kadvani
authors.institution: Charotar University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Grasping and Stabilizing Tumbling Objects with Rotating-Base Multi-Arm Space Manipulators
papers.abstract: This paper presents an innovative guidance and control method for a space manipulator that actively maneuvers its base to hold a tumbling object stationary relative to the base during proximity operations. This simplifies motion planning, reduces collision risk, and enables impact-free capture using single- or multi-arm configurations, with or without predefined grasping interfaces. The proposed approach involves two phases. In the pre-grasping phase, a synchronization control aligns the target's center of mass (CoM) with the system's instantaneous center of rotation (ICR), virtually rigidizing the target-servicer system to keep the object stationary for reliable grasping. In the post grasping phase, a control strategy based on Hamiltonian dynamics and optimal control stabilizes the combined system by minimizing time, fuel, or energy, while respecting base torque limits and multiple grasping constraints. For structured targets, applied forces and torques stay within their bounds; for unstructured ones, friction constraints prevent slipping. A case study demonstrates the method's effectiveness in enabling both the subsequent grasping and detumbling phases.

papers.title: LiSA: Linear Stochastic Attention for Long-Range Visual Modeling
papers.abstract: Self-attention has become the standard for modern sequence modeling, enabling Transformers to model long-range dependencies across a wide range of modalities. Despite these advances, its quadratic cost with respect to sequence length remains a significant computational bottleneck. Recent work addresses this limitation by introducing linear variants of self-attention, namely with kernel approximations of the softmax operator. However, their first-order aggregation restricts expressivity and struggles to capture higher-order structure. We propose Linear Stochastic Attention (LiSA), a linear attention plug-in module that enables higher-order token interactions via a stochastic diffusion process based on truncated random walks. LiSA incorporates adaptive locality, favoring semantically similar neighbors to preserve fine-grained structures, while maintaining stable and efficient training. We conduct extensive experiments on classification, semantic segmentation, and object detection tasks and show improved results over state-of-the-art methods.
