papers.title: Why strong spin-orbit coupling does not destabilize the Dirac spin liquid in the Yb delafossites
papers.abstract: The Yb delafossites NaYbSe$_2$, KYbSe$_2$, CsYbSe$_2$ and NaYbO$_2$ are candidates for the U(1) Dirac spin liquid (DSL) of the triangular lattice. Strong spin-orbit coupling gives their exchange an XXZ anisotropy $\Delta$ and bond-dependent couplings $J_{\pm\pm}$, $J_{z\pm}$ that lock the spin frame to the lattice. We show that, within a single layer of a stable Heisenberg DSL, these couplings generate no relevant Lorentz-scalar operator of their own. Inversion at the bond centers removes the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya channel that gaps the kagome DSL, so the locked symmetry forbids a mass, density or current at any order and, assuming continuity, any new monopole term through charge three. Every Lorentz-scalar four-fermion operator induced by spin-orbit coupling shares an SU(4) multiplet, and hence its scaling dimension, with a Heisenberg-allowed one, and the nine non-scalar quartics without such a partner arise only at second order and are irrelevant at large $N$. The Heisenberg DSL itself allows a Lorentz-vector quartic of large-$N$ dimension 2.92, which a stable phase must also render irrelevant. Beyond a single layer, spin-orbit coupling opens an interlayer monopole channel in rhombohedral stacking. If the Heisenberg DSL is instead multicritical, an anisotropy as small as that of KYbSe$_2$ matters only below tens of mK. At the transition to 120$^\circ$ order the anisotropy is relevant, and exact diagonalization indicates that easy-plane anisotropy selects the chiral-Ising class. Existing KYbSe$_2$ neutron data below $J$ do not yet fix the K-point exponent, and gapless out-of-plane spin fluctuations at the K point would test the chiral-Ising selection.

papers.title: Spin-orbit-locked symmetry and the stability of the triangular Dirac spin liquid in the ytterbium delafossites
papers.abstract: The Yb delafossites NaYbSe$_2$, KYbSe$_2$, CsYbSe$_2$ and NaYbO$_2$ are candidates for the triangular U(1) Dirac spin liquid, QED$_3$ with $N_f=4$, but their exchange is spin-orbit coupled. Under their spin-orbit-locked space group we determine which operators the XXZ anisotropy and the bond-dependent couplings $J_{\pm\pm}$, $J_{z\pm}$ induce, and at what order. Symmetry forbids every Dirac mass, density and current at any order and, assuming adiabatic continuity, any new monopole term through charge three. At linear order the couplings reach only spin-2 members of the quartic multiplets $\mathbf{20}'$ and $\mathbf{84}$, which share their dimensions with Heisenberg-allowed operators. At second order $J_{\pm\pm}$ and $J_{z\pm}$ renormalize the anisotropy through $J_{z\pm}^2-2J_{\pm\pm}^2$, and nine spin-1 quartics without Heisenberg partners appear, irrelevant at $O(1/N)$. A single layer of a stable Heisenberg spin liquid thus acquires no relevant Lorentz-scalar operator from spin-orbit coupling. The Heisenberg liquid itself allows a Lorentz-vector $\mathbf{20}'$ quartic of large-$N$ dimension 2.92, with two-loop $\epsilon$-expansion estimates 2.9-3.5. Rhombohedral stacking adds triplet-monopole tunneling between layers at first order. At the transition to 120$^\circ$ order the anisotropy is relevant, with crossover exponent $y_T\simeq0.74$-1, and exact diagonalization shows that easy-plane anisotropy selects the chiral-Ising class. The out-of-plane spectrum at the K point then stays gapless, and the spin-flip to non-spin-flip ratio grows as $\omega^{-0.56}$ at leading order. Existing KYbSe$_2$ neutron data below $J$ do not fix the K-point exponent. In-plane fields induce a chiral mass and an out-of-plane moment proportional to $\sin3\varphi$, zero along the bonds and canceling between CsYbSe$_2$ layers, which the planar thermal Hall effect can test.

papers.title: Large Language Model-Assisted Adaptive Heuristic Search for Agile Earth Observation Satellite Scheduling
papers.abstract: Agile Earth observation satellites must coordinate imaging tasks within limited observation windows, while accounting for attitude maneuvering and onboard energy constraints. Competition among observation opportunities makes scheduling performance sensitive to the heuristic rules used for task selection. This letter proposes a large language model (LLM)-assisted adaptive heuristic search method for agile Earth observation satellite scheduling. The LLM generates an initial heuristic rule according to the characteristics of the scheduling instance. During the subsequent ant colony search, search performance and scheduling information are fed back to the LLM to refine the heuristic rule. The proposed modifications are evaluated through paired solution constructions before being incorporated into the search process. A unified scheduling procedure determines task selection, satellite assignment, and observation timing under the operational constraints. Experiments on six scheduling scenarios involving 50--200 imaging tasks demonstrate that the proposed method achieves 4.3\%--9.6\% higher mean observation benefit than the strongest baseline.

papers.title: Who is the Pronoun Pro? Comparing LLMs and Humans at Number-Disambiguation of 'they'
papers.abstract: This study evaluates whether large language models (LLMs) can reliably replace or complement human research assistants in linguistically complex annotation. In a controlled annotation task, 73 human annotators (local students and crowdworkers with and without a background in linguistics) and more than 40 LLM configurations number-disambiguated 174 authentic uses of 'they' from Reddit, including innovative and context-sensitive cases. The best LLM, Kimi K3, reached 94.5% accuracy, above the human majority vote (86.2%) and the mean of the top half of human annotators (78.5%); only the single best human annotator scored higher (95.7%). LLMs also offer substantial practical advantages in cost and speed. However, qualitative error analysis reveals a crucial complementarity: human reasoning in low-agreement cases exposes inconsistencies in the annotation typology and thereby improves the methodological framework itself. The study contributes (i) a benchmark-style human-LLM comparison for a semantically demanding task, (ii) transparent cost and time evidence, and (iii) a methodological argument against a purely replacement-oriented view of automation. LLMs are viable for large-scale annotation support in linguistics, but their responsible use requires human critical oversight. The dataset with its gold-standard labels, all human and LLM annotations, and the fully reproducible code are openly available as a Quarto-based, public repository.

papers.title: Convex ribbon disks, quasipositivity, and Lagrangian sliceness
papers.abstract: We introduce a version of convex surface theory for immersed ribbon surfaces with Legendrian boundary. As an application, we establish a special case of K3: Problem 1.70 on sharpness in the slice-Bennequin inequality implying quasipositivity, and a special case of a conjecture of Cornwell, Ng, and Sivek on characterizing Lagrangian sliceness. Specifically, we prove that if $K$ is a knot that bounds a "star-shaped" ribbon disk and satisfies $\overline{\mathrm{sl}}(K) = -1$ (resp.\ $\overline{\mathrm{tb}}(K) = -1$), then $K$ is quasipositive (resp.\ Lagrangian slice). In fact, we prove these statements for any fixed transverse (resp.\ Legendrian) representative.

papers.title: From Forecasting to Feedback: Evaluating Learned Dynamics for Tokamak Control
papers.abstract: Learned temporal models are moving beyond offline forecasting toward interactive environments for decision making, yet logged-trajectory accuracy need not predict closed-loop behavior under policies optimized in the learned model. This forecasting-control gap matters in tokamak magnetic control, where coupled plasma-circuit dynamics and actuator constraints can amplify errors through feedback. Using a calibrated free-boundary Grad-Shafranov solver, we collect four datasets in a 2x2 design over physics-parameter and current-reference coverage. At matched budgets of 500, 1k, 3k, and 5k rollouts, we train 16 action-conditioned Transformers; PPO policies optimized in the 5k surrogates are then evaluated without adaptation on six reference-solver conditions. Only joint-coverage D4 shows monotonically decreasing cross-condition mean error, whereas D1 improves in distribution but degrades out of distribution. Binary completion masks substantial closed-loop differences: D2-D4 each complete 83.3% of conditions, but reach on average 99.0%, 94.7%, and 90.5% of the evaluation horizon, while their worst conditions reach 94.2%, 68.2%, and 43.2%. Policies trained with action noise complete 5/24 matched conditions, compared with 19/24 under nominal training, and have a lower mean horizon-capped episode length. Based on one trained policy per configuration and one evaluation realization per condition, the results support combining prediction error, episode completion, condition-level duration, and tracking quality.

papers.title: Hierarchical Intelligent Evolutionary Optimization for UAV-Assisted NOMA-MEC Systems
papers.abstract: The integration of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), mobile edge computing (MEC) and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) provides an effective solution for computation-intensive and latency-sensitive services in infrastructure-deficient environments. However, the joint optimization of UAV trajectories, task offloading, communication and computing resources under heterogeneous task priorities results in a highly coupled mixed-integer non-convex problem. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Hierarchical Intelligent Evolutionary Algorithm (HIEA) for priority-aware multi-UAV cooperative NOMA-MEC networks, which integrates multi-head deep Q-network (MH-DQN)-based intelligent decision generation, communication-aware initialization, adaptive evolutionary exploration and successive convex approximation (SCA)-based precision refinement. Specifically, a novel communication-aware initialization mechanism, termed Channel Quality Indicator (CQI)-guided Load-Aware Trajectory Initialization (CQI-LATI), is designed to incorporate CQI and task workload characteristics into evolutionary population construction, generating high-quality and diversity-preserving initial populations. Theoretical analysis characterizes HIEA's search-space reduction, the quality-diversity trade-off of CQI-guided initialization, and the accuracy-efficiency trade-off of SCA refinement, and extensive simulations demonstrate that HIEA outperforms benchmark schemes, with gains of up to 6.5% in throughput, 13.6% in task completion rate and 15.3% in energy efficiency.

papers.title: Friedman--Stanley cofinality without Borel completeness
papers.abstract: Friedman and Stanley asked whether an invariant Borel class of countable structures must be Borel complete whenever every countable level of their hierarchy reduces to it. We construct a counterexample in one fixed countable language. The structural counterexample and its principal supporting results have been formalized in Lean~4 and it is available on github.

papers.title: Cycle WAM: Coupling Action and Video through Cycle Consistency
papers.abstract: Recent advances in video modeling have driven substantial progress in world action models (WAMs). Existing approaches exploit pretrained video priors by decoding actions from latent representations or inferring them from generated videos. The underlying link is causal: robot actions produce changes in the scene, and video observations of these changes provide evidence for inferring the actions that produced them. However, existing training formulations do not by themselves ensure that actions and their predicted visual consequences are consistent, potentially limiting the use of pretrained capabilities. We treat video and action as paired modalities linked by this causal relationship and learn their correspondence through a unified training framework designed to better exploit pretrained video priors. Cycle WAM first augments video-action co-training with bidirectional conversion to reinforce cross-modal correspondence and recover forward and inverse dynamics. It then introduces a differentiable cycle-reconstruction objective to further couple the two mappings. The resulting model supports both forward and inverse dynamics, with the potential to improve performance through more effective use of pretrained video priors. Cycle WAM achieves state-of-the-art performance among comparable methods on LIBERO-Pro and substantially improves DreamZero on DROID. Comparisons with UWM characterize its inverse-dynamics performance and show sharper visual detail in the displayed forward-dynamics predictions.

papers.title: Asymptotic Optimality of $c\mu$-Rule for LLM Inference Scheduling under Memory Constraint
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference, the process by which a pre-trained model receives an input prompt and generates output tokens sequentially, has become increasingly important with the widespread deployment of LLM-based applications. As inference workloads continue to scale, GPU memory has emerged as a critical bottleneck: the long input prompts and generation sequences common in agentic and reasoning workloads lead to substantial key-value (KV) cache usage. In this paper, we study the resulting online scheduling problem from a queueing perspective. Requests arrive stochastically with heterogeneous prompt and output lengths, undergo prefill and autoregressive decode, and compete for a finite KV-cache capacity. Unlike classical queueing models, the duration of a processing step depends on both prefill computation and KV-cache I/O, so service capacity is jointly determined by computation, memory access, and memory occupancy. We develop a fluid model that reduces the system to a multiclass single-server queue with effective service rates capturing computation, memory access, and memory capacity. This fluid analysis yields a $c\mu$ priority rule, where the effective service rate $\mu$ is jointly determined by computational speed, memory bandwidth, and memory capacity. We prove that this rule minimizes cumulative holding cost in the fluid model and, for a finite workload, also minimizes completion time and maximizes full-run output-token throughput. We then construct a feasible scheduling policy for the original finite system and prove that its scaled dynamics converge to the optimal fluid policy. Finally, experiments on a real LLM serving engine using an NVIDIA H800 show that practical implementations of the proposed priority rule substantially reduce average latency while maintaining high throughput relative to existing scheduling policies.

authors.name: Nian Si
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Tropical Cyclone-Following Dataset for Limited-Area Machine Learning Applications
papers.abstract: This work presents a lightweight dataset of tropical cyclone (TC)-following meteorological variables to facilitate the development and application of machine learning (ML) methods in TC research. Using outputs from our previous climate downscaling and idealized simulations, the dataset is constructed as multichannel video sequences that track TC centers throughout their lifetimes. To demonstrate the dataset utility, we present an application in which a regional ML model is trained to predict TC intensity with explicit incorporation of lateral boundary conditions. Our results highlight the importance of lateral boundary information for predicting TC intensity with ML models inside a limited-area domain, underscoring the need to properly account for lateral boundaries when developing regional ML models for TC intensity forecast.

authors.name: Minh-Khanh Luong
authors.institution: Trường Đại học Khoa học và Công nghệ Hà Nội

papers.title: Hydrogen Electron Cyclotron Resonance Dissociator Demonstrator for the Project 8 Experiment
papers.abstract: Project 8, a neutrino mass experiment, employs the novel frequency technique of cyclotron radiation emission spectroscopy (CRES) to perform a model independent measurement of neutrino mass via tritium beta decay. Our pioneering experiment will consist of a beamline that dissociates molecular tritium, surface cools atoms through accommodation, evaporatively cools and slows atoms, and traps them in a CRES resonant cavity to advance towards our sensitivity goal of 40 meV/c^2 for our final electron-weighted neutrino mass measurement. We are prototyping an electron cyclotron resonance (ECR) dissociator that uses a tunable 1 kW 2.45 GHz RF generator and electromagnets to ignite a hydrogen plasma in an aluminum resonant cavity. Our ECR source is designed to produce a high atom flux (~10^19 atoms/second) near room temperature. We present the engineering development, gas diagnostics, and spectroscopy data from our hydrogen plasma.

papers.title: FP4Quant: Efficient 4-Bit Communication Compression for Model-Parallel LLM Training
papers.abstract: The rapid scaling of large language models (LLMs) has made communication overhead a critical bottleneck in distributed model-parallel training. Although existing low-precision compression methods can effectively reduce communication costs, further reducing the communication footprint to ultra-low-bit formats such as FP4 introduces new challenges, including limited numerical range, sub-byte storage overhead, and increased computational cost from fine-grained quantization. In this paper, we present \textbf{FP4Quant}, a micro-grouped FP4 compression framework for efficient model-parallel LLM training. FP4Quant integrates a micro-grouped dual-scale FP4 quantization mechanism to preserve local tensor distribution characteristics, a warp-cooperative FP4 packing scheme to enable efficient sub-byte data representation, and a hybrid two-level FWHT pipeline to mitigate quantization errors with GPU-aware execution optimization. Experiments on NVIDIA H100 GPUs with Qwen-7B demonstrate up to 1.56$\times$ end-to-end throughput improvement over BF16, revealing a trade-off between throughput and model quality.

papers.title: Beyond Compression Ratio: High-Throughput KV Compression for Disaggregated LLM Serving
papers.abstract:
KV cache compression reduces the communication volume of disaggregated large language model serving, but its practical benefit depends not only on compression ratio and model quality, but also on how efficiently the compression pipeline executes. This requirement becomes increasingly important as modern serving systems adopt high-bandwidth interconnects, where inefficient compression can offset a substantial portion of the saved communication time.
  This paper presents \system, a high-throughput KV cache compression data path built on top of \kvserve. \system improves compression execution in two complementary ways. First, it fuses the distribution transformation and low-bit quantization stages into a KV-aware \tilelang kernel, eliminating intermediate tensor materialization and redundant memory accesses. Second, it replaces the original lossless compression backend with an open, extensible, and searchable backend based on \lc, enabling high-performance compression operator pipelines. The fused kernel achieves up to $5.9\times$ speedup, while the new lossless backend increases compression throughput from below 90~GB/s to over 500~GB/s. Across the evaluated workloads, \system reduces job completion time by up to $2.04\times$. End-to-end evaluation shows that these optimizations allow KV compression to retain meaningful communication benefits under modern high-bandwidth network.

authors.name: Zedong Liu
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Yuhan Chen
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Convergence analysis of TriCG and TriMR for symmetric quasi-definite linear systems
papers.abstract: TriCG and TriMR are two short-recurrence iterative methods introduced by Montoison and Orban [SIAM J.\ Sci.\ Comput., 43 (2021), pp.\ A2502--A2525] for solving symmetric quasi-definite linear systems. Extensive numerical experiments have demonstrated the efficiency of these two methods, but a systematic convergence analysis is still lacking. In this paper, we derive convergence bounds for the TriCG error norm and the TriMR residual norm. Numerical experiments support the theoretical results.

papers.title: Fractional colorings of $K_r$-free graphs with local demands
papers.abstract:
We study fractional coloring with local demands, a framework introduced by Kelly and Postle in which one seeks a probability distribution on the independent sets of a graph such that each vertex $v$ is included with probability at least a prescribed target $\phi(v)$. For $K_r$-free graphs, Kelly and Postle conjectured that such a distribution exists provided $\phi(v)\le c_r\frac{\log d(v)}{d(v)}$ for a fixed \(c_r>0\), where $d(v)$ is the degree of $v$, and they established this up to a factor of $(\log\log d(v))^2$. In this paper, we prove their conjecture, showing that \[
  \phi(v)\le\frac{c}{r}\frac{\log(d(v)+2)}{d(v)+1} \] suffices for an absolute constant $c>0$. As a corollary, we obtain a lower bound on the independence number of $K_r$-free graphs in terms of their degree sequence. This strengthens the bound that OpenAI proved in resolving the Ajtai-Erd\H{o}s-Koml\'os-Szemer\'edi conjecture. Moreover, our argument yields a deterministic algorithm that produces the desired probability distribution in time $2^{O(r^2)}n^{O(1)}$, where \(n\) is the number of vertices and the implied constants are absolute.

papers.title: Sample-Grained Approximate Unlearning with Provable Per-Sample Bounds
papers.abstract: Machine unlearning aims to erase the influence of a designated forget set from a trained model while preserving strong utility on the retain set. Approximate unlearning methods efficiently achieve this goal without full retraining, but their effectiveness is primarily assessed using dataset-level aggregate metrics. These aggregate metrics can mask deviations from retraining at the level of individual samples. In this work, we focus on per-sample unlearning effectiveness. We introduce SALA (Sample-grained Likelihoods ALignment), a plug-in optimization framework that enables approximate unlearning methods to operate at the level of individual samples by steering each example toward its correct target distribution. To quantitatively assess this behavior, we further propose the sample-grained distribution gap, a metric that captures per-sample discrepancies between approximate unlearning and exact retraining output distributions. We provide theoretical guarantees showing that SALA contracts this gap and yields a bounded per-sample discrepancy to retraining. To make this framework practical, we develop a low-cost estimation method for the member and non-member target distributions. Extensive experiments on classification and generation tasks demonstrate that SALA reduces the sample-grained distribution gap by up to $86.67\%$ when paired with existing approximate unlearning baselines, while also improving robustness to unlearning hyperparameters.

papers.title: Best-of-Depth: Learning Exploratory Dynamics in Looped Transformers
papers.abstract: Looped Transformers extend inference-time computation through repeated latent-state updates, but final-depth training does not directly encourage useful intermediate alternatives. We introduce Best-of-Depth (BoD), which trains a recurrent trajectory as a candidate set by minimizing prediction loss across depths. Different valid targets can be matched at different depths without architectural changes or depth-specific labels. An exact-match analysis connects this objective to solution coverage. On N-Queens completion and graph coloring, BoD improves coverage over final-depth and intermediate-supervision objectives. N-Queens coverage reaches 91.03%, versus 45.75% for final-depth training. Further experiments show discovery beyond the training depth and recovery of solutions withheld from teacher pools on familiar inputs. Fine-tuning a pretrained looped language model with BoD yields higher pooled code-generation success than final-depth training when programs are generated separately at evaluated fixed depths. These results support training recurrent computation for solution discovery along its trajectory.

papers.title: On flow unsteadiness in strongly separated high-speed ramp flows using kinetic and data-driven methods
papers.abstract: The gas dynamics of high speed flows over several compression-expansion ramp geometries with large separation regions were investigated using a particle kinetic approach and data driven methods. These large separation regions allow study of the role of scaled angle predicted by triple deck theory on recirculation strength, separation size, and appearance of secondary recirculation regions, all of which lead to flow unsteadiness. Examining four different free stream conditions for the same geometry using the direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) approach, we show that the stability of single recirculation in the separation region is more sensitive to wall temperature and free stream velocity than physical ramp angle. Stability in this context refers to appearance of secondary separation regions. In addition, configurations with similar types of recirculation regions from literature considered, we find that general trends regarding unsteadiness, such as appearance of secondary recirculation regions, mostly hold; however, the flows are too complex to be characterized by only scaled angle. Thus, stochastic flowfields generated by DSMC were investigated using data driven methods, namely spectral proper orthogonal decomposition and dynamic mode decomposition. We found that both methods yield similar frequency components and mode shapes for spatio-temporal coherent structures of unsteady DSMC flows. With the help of these structures, the main mechanisms of unsteadiness were identified as oscillations of the reattachment shock, Kelvin-Helmholtz like instability of the shear layer, and c-shaped mode of the separation bubble. This is the first time SPOD has been applied to a DSMC generated flowfield and compared with DMD.

papers.title: On the Complexity of Finite-Sum Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization with Exact Proximal Oracles
papers.abstract: Finite-sum nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax problems arise in adversarial training and distributionally robust learning. Their known lower bounds cover only linear-span algorithms, zero-respecting algorithms, or a restricted proximal protocol. They leave open the power of exact component proximal steps, whose responses are global saddle points of regularized component problems and can expose directions that gradients do not reveal. We show that neither unrestricted adaptivity nor exact proximal access improves the polynomial complexity. We consider $n$ components with joint mean-squared smoothness $L$ and condition number $\kappa$, started from a point with primal gap at most $\Delta$ and joint gradient norm at most $\sqrt{2L\Delta}$. For $\varepsilon^2/(L\Delta)$ below a universal constant, every randomized adaptive algorithm with exact component values, gradients, and proximal responses needs $\Omega(n+\min\{\sqrt n\,\kappa,n^{3/4}\sqrt\kappa\}L\Delta/\varepsilon^2)$ component queries in the worst case to find an $\varepsilon$-stationary point of the value function. A method using only component gradients attains this rate up to a factor $\log^2(2+\kappa)$, including initialization. Zhou (arXiv:2610.04944) concurrently proves the same rate for zero-respecting first-order methods. In our hard instances, every component admits proximal steps with the same step sizes, and a response for a component reveals hidden directions only up to the first one assigned to another component.

authors.name: Yuxing Peng
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Information Loss Is All You Need: $TC^0$ Pseudorandomness from Worst-Case Lattices
papers.abstract:
Can deterministic information loss yield post-quantum pseudorandomness with $TC^0$ evaluation? We show that deterministic rounding achieves this under quantum worst-case lattice hardness, with fixed polynomial parameters and no predetermined sample bound.
  We introduce learning with algebraic rounding (LAR), which applies an explicit integer rounding map to blocks of secret-dependent linear measurements and encodes the result in a lattice quotient. For one fixed family with polynomially bounded modulus and dimensions, deterministic labels on exactly uniform, secret-independent public matrices are computationally indistinguishable from independent uniform labels for every polynomial number of classical random examples. Our classical reduction from Gaussian LWE, combined with the quantum worst-case reduction to LWE, bases LAR on GapSVP and SIVP over general lattices at approximation factor $\widetilde{O}(q)$, where $q$ is the modulus.
  The proof uses source-independent affine transport: public affine maps sampled independently of the hidden errors transport the Gaussian error law close to uniform on the rounding map's zero-label fiber while preserving exactly uniform public matrices. For every fixed inverse-polynomial accuracy, we give a polynomial-time sampler for the same public parameter family.
  This yields the first post-quantum weak pseudorandom function with joint key-and-input evaluation in $TC^0$, secure against uniform quantum polynomial-time distinguishers given any polynomial number of classical uniform random examples. We also prove hardness of learning polynomial-size two-hidden-layer ReLU networks from noiseless uniform random examples, even for quantum polynomial-time improper learners.

papers.title: Overdetermined boundary problems for maximal graphs
papers.abstract: We study overdetermined boundary problems for the maximal surface equation with zero Dirichlet data and constant nonzero Neumann data . For the exterior of a bounded domain with connected boundary in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq2$, we prove that such domain must be the complement of a ball and the solution is radial. In dimension two, we also show that a positive solution on a domain bounded by a properly embedded noncompact connected curve forces the domain to be a half-plane and the solution to be affine. The proofs combine the divergence structure of the equation with the induced geometry of maximal graphs.

papers.title: A Compact Residual-Screened Local Reduced-Order Model for Diffuse-Domain Shape Optimization
papers.abstract: We generalize the compact residual-screened local reduced-order model (CL-ROM) from Brinkman-penalized flow to shape optimization with the diffuse domain method (DDM). As with Brinkman penalization, DDM extends evolving-domain problems to a fixed rectangular domain, allowing one grid for discretization and directly compatible snapshots from different designs. Unlike Brinkman penalization, DDM uses a phase field to weight operators and sources and treats Dirichlet, Neumann and Robin conditions through diffuse boundary terms. The CL-ROM mechanism carries over: recent full-order and corrected solutions determine local reduced spaces, while residual screening, correction with retained factors and objective verification decide when a full-order solve is needed. We derive reduced operators, residuals and sensitivities for each diffuse model, using Galerkin projection for the symmetric problems and least-squares Petrov--Galerkin projection for nonlinear flow. For the symmetric problems we prove a local approximation estimate that admits inexact, corrected snapshots. In numerical tests of shape identification, drag minimization in Navier--Stokes channel flow and compliance minimization of a cantilever, CL-ROM uses reduced solutions for nearly all design updates, reproduces the full-order objectives with relative differences below $5\times10^{-6}$, and is $3.85$ to $7.65$ times faster than a full-order baseline that reuses factorizations as preconditioners.

authors.name: Zhu Wang
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: How Agent Skills Evolve: A Large-Scale Empirical Study of Skills on GitHub
papers.abstract: Large language model-based agents increasingly rely on external skills to reuse task-specific knowledge without retraining the model. As skills become common for extending agent capabilities, understanding creation and evolution is critical for reliable agent systems. However, existing studies mainly examine agent skills from a static perspective, leaving their evolution in real-world repositories largely unexplored. This limits our understanding of the patterns and motivations behind skill changes. To fill this gap, we present a large-scale empirical study of agent skills, capturing 84,200 skills and 750,898 commits from GitHub. We manually construct taxonomies of skill components, change patterns, and evolution motivations, and build an automated annotation pipeline to label changes at scale. Based on the taxonomy, we conduct quantitative analyses of skill composition and post-creation evolution frequency, together with qualitative assessments of modified components, change patterns, and motivations. Our findings reveal five implications: (i) reliability receives less attention in skill composition and change, motivating execution-contract skill design that incorporates verification and recovery mechanisms; (ii) evolution changes concentrate in project-coupled skills, calling for automated just-in-time skill updating mechanisms; (iii) change patterns are dominated by incremental enrichment and refinement, motivating pattern-guided skill enhancers that diagnose and improve incomplete skill components; (iv) redundancy is a practical maintenance issue, highlighting the need for context-efficient skill representation; (v) security-motivated changes show limited risk reduction, suggesting skill regression testing methods that objectively verify skill functionality and security. Beyond these insights, our dataset provides a basis for future studies on automated skill techniques.

authors.name: Jialun Cao
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

authors.name: Shing-Chi Cheung
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

papers.title: Constraining the Superconducting Gap of Monolayer FeSe/SrTiO$_3$ via Statistical Analysis and Tip-Height-Dependent Tunneling Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Monolayer FeSe grown on SrTiO$_3$ (001) exemplifies interface-enhanced superconductivity, exhibiting a transition temperature nearly ten times that of bulk FeSe. Yet, its tunneling spectra lack clearly identifiable superconducting coherence peaks, preventing an unambiguous determination of the gap magnitude. Here, we use ultralow-temperature scanning tunneling spectroscopy as a function of temperature, tip-sample separation, and lateral position to disentangle tunneling contributions by statistical analysis. Decay rates extracted by regression of tip-height-dependent spectroscopy reveal three energy regimes: Andreev-reflection-dominated tunneling below 6 meV, mixed Andreev and quasiparticle tunneling between 6 and 13 meV, and predominantly quasiparticle tunneling above 13 meV. Spatially resolved spectroscopy and correlation analysis further reveal that the tunneling conductance is predominantly localized near defects below 6 meV but becomes spatially extended at higher energies. Together, these results constrain the superconducting gap to lie between 6 and 13 meV. Our findings establish statistical analysis of spectroscopy as a powerful approach to constraining superconducting gap structures when complex spectral features prevent the unambiguous identification of coherence peaks.

papers.title: FourSight: Stable FP4 RL Post-Training via Sequence Filtering and Sparse Channel Compensation
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training increasingly targets low-bit deployment, with NVFP4 weight-and activation quantization (W4A4) becoming the state-of-the-practice format. However, integrating NVFP4 into RL degrades rollout quality and amplifies cross-engine training-inference mismatch (TIM), destabilizing training. We show that these failures are concentrated rather than uniform - severely mismatched tail tokens concentrate in a few outlier sequences, while policy weights remain largely intact and quantization error concentrates in a few high-variance activation channels. Guided by this, we present FourSight, an algorithm-system co-design with two targeted solutions: TIM-aware sequence filtering that excludes drifted trajectories from policy updates, and sparse precision compensation that keeps only top-variance channels in BF16 while retaining native NVFP4 elsewhere. We further design a fused SpliceGEMM kernel with specialized prefill and decode datapaths to minimize overhead. FourSight sustains near-BF16 accuracy and strong FP4 deployment quality across models and engines, while improving step-to-accuracy by 1.76-2.60x and staying within 2.3% of FP4 step time up to 120B-scale models.

authors.name: Xiaowen Chu
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

papers.title: Large deviation of preimages of points under the dynamics of a holomorphic correspondence
papers.abstract: Our main objective in this paper is to prove a large deviation result for the distribution of preimages of a point under the iteration of a holomorphic correspondence with respect to the unique equilibrium state associated to a H\"{o}lder continuous potential defined on the support of the Dinh-Sibony measure of the correspondence. As a consequence, we obtain a convergence result which generalises the result on equidistribution of preimages by Dinh and Sibony. We also study a situation where the Dinh-Sibony measure happens to be the unique measure of maximal entropy for an appropriate holomorphic correspondence and also record some comments that connect this work with some recent works in the literature.

authors.name: Bharath Krishna Seshadri
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Thiruvananthapuram

authors.name: Shrihari Sridharan
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Thiruvananthapuram

papers.title: Are LLM Research Agents Reliable Judges of Predictability? Evidence from Planted-Signal Worlds
papers.abstract: Researchers ask large language model (LLM) research agents whether a forecasting model beats a static benchmark, a verdict that real data cannot check. We treat the agent as a statistical test and score pre-specified runs of three frontier models and one open-weight model in simulated worlds with a planted signal. The agents detect weak signals more often than a pre-specified out-of-sample test, mainly because they accept weaker evidence: held to an agent's false-positive rate, a conventional in-sample test does as well or better. The agents claim predictability too often in worlds without a signal, state miscalibrated probabilities, and change their verdicts after a sentence about prior research; the magnitudes depend on the model. The excess false claims persist in simulated worlds without a resampling artifact. Agent verdicts are informative but need a neutral brief, a decision rule fixed outside the agent and a sealed holdout.

papers.title: Averaging Collusion Breaks Traceability in Personalized Neural Audio Watermarking
papers.abstract: Personalized neural audio watermarking systems embed user-specific payloads into audio to trace the user associated with a leaked or misused copy. Existing evaluations mainly assume access to a single personalized copy, but real-world distribution may expose multiple copies of the same recording. We find that simple sample-wise averaging breaks traceability: averaging only two copies produces tracing-failure rates of 87.7-99.7% across the five systems while largely preserving audio quality. Decoder outputs show distinct responses to coalition payload composition across systems, with high majority agreement in TimbreWM but substantially lower agreement in WMCodec. In a more sophisticated payload-aware setting, mixture weighting can further steer the decoder toward a selected nonmember, achieving a target success rate of 92.3% in TimbreWM. Preliminary confidence screening rejects many collusion-induced assignments while retaining most valid single-copy outputs. Code and results are available at https://github.com/Silwan5z/neural-audio-watermark-collusion-attack. This work highlights multi-copy traceability as an additional evaluation dimension for personalized neural audio watermarking alongside conventional single-copy robustness.

papers.title: MCPGuard: Finding Conformance Gaps in MCP SDKs via Dual-Track Analysis and Dynamic Adjudication
papers.abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects large language model agents to external tools and services through official SDKs that implement message validation and session logic. Specification constraints omitted by these SDKs may propagate to downstream applications, highlighting the importance of SDK-level conformance testing. Yet existing MCP conformance tools mainly exercise running endpoints and reveal little about whether SDK models enforce specification requirements. We present MCPGuard, an automated LLM-based framework for detecting specification-to-SDK conformance gaps. Its structural track aligns JSON Schema constraints with normalized SDK models and produces constraint-specific evidence. Its behavioral track extracts normative prose rules, retrieves bounded function-level slices, and audits them with LLMs for candidate omissions. An evidence-aware dynamic adjudicator then inspects complete source context and builds PoCs to validate candidates. A shared kernel with language-specific adapters enables analysis across SDKs. On the official Python 1.26.0 and TypeScript 1.29.0 SDKs, MCPGuard confirms 13 and 19 findings, respectively, none of which are exposed by two black-box baselines. Tests on open MCP servers further show that these gaps can systematically propagate downstream. By making SDK conformance of specification constraints directly testable, MCPGuard complements conventional endpoint-oriented conformance suites.

authors.name: Yawen Zheng
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Minimal model of a Plateau-Rayleigh instability of a solid binary alloy nanowire: impacts of surface segregation
papers.abstract: Minimal model and its linear stability analysis (LSA) for Plateau-Rayleigh (PR) instability of an intermixed, solid binary alloy nanowire is presented. Model accounts only for the surface diffusions of the alloy components without anisotropies of a surface energies, and for a classical thermodynamic surface segregation. Model allows to assess a deviation of a longwave instability cutoff wavelength $\lambda_c$ from the classical value $2\pi r_0$ (a wire circumference) as a function of a surface composition deviation from its equilibrium value, a wire radius, and a bulk concentration of a minority component. Results of LSA are presented for AuNi, PtNi, and CoNi nanowires, where an important distinction is that a surface segregation curve for CoNi is qualitatively different from the one for AuNi and PtNi. For each nanowire there is a sizable region of a parameter space where $\lambda_c<2\pi r_0$ and correspondingly, a fastest growing perturbation wavelength $\lambda_{max}$ is also less than a wire circumference. This is in stark contrast to PR instability of a single-component nanowire transporting mass by surface diffusion - in this case $\lambda_c$ and $\lambda_{max}$ are larger than a wire circumference. Strong surface segregation is primarily responsible for unusually small $\lambda_c$ and $\lambda_{max}$. Results suggest that a large number of small and closely spaced nanoparticles may emerge upon disintegration via annealing of a binary alloy nanowire.

papers.title: Timely Ground-Station Status Delivery via UAV-Assisted Data Collection and Hierarchical RL
papers.abstract: We consider a UAV-assisted status-update system in which a rotary-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) collects updates from multiple sensors, stores the newest update of each sensor, and forwards selected buffered updates to a ground station (GS). We minimize a weighted sum of the time-average GS-side age of information (AoI) and UAV energy consumption over a finite horizon. The optimization is subject to half-duplex operation, sensor and UAV energy-causality constraints, transmission-rate and power limits, and a terminal-location constraint. Because collection changes the information age at the UAV but does not reduce the GS-side AoI until the buffered update is forwarded, mobility, collection, and forwarding decisions are coupled over time. We use a hierarchical AoI-energy actor-critic (HAE-AC) controller in which a coarse-timescale actor selects return-feasible UAV movements, while a deterministic per-slot scheduler constructs feasible collection or forwarding sets and assigns the minimum transmit power required for each scheduled transmission. In a 100-sensor deployment, HAE-AC reduces the average GS-side AoI by about 22% relative to an adaptive staleness-gated benchmark. Compared with forward-upon-collection, selective buffered forwarding reduces the number of downlink bursts by roughly 30% while increasing the number of collections per sensor by more than 23%.

papers.title: Balance in Inequality: Testing the Physical Equilibrium, Precession, and Structural Stability of Magic Gems
papers.abstract: A magic square exemplifies balance in inequality: its $n^2$ entries $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ are distinct, yet every row, column, and main diagonal sums to $\mu_n=n(n^2+1)/2$. Lifting centred grid cells into $\mathbb{R}^3$ as radial vectors $\mathbf{p}_{ij}(\lambda)=(x_j,y_i,\lambda z_{ij})$ and taking their convex hull---the Magic Gem $\mathcal{G}_\lambda(S)$---asks: when does line-sum equality suffice for equilibrium in 3D, and when a nonlinear realization breaks balance, how can an opposing inequality restore it? We test this across all $880$ order-$4$ magic squares in four regimes. For radial spokes from $O$, natural lengths balance identically, while unit spokes break equilibrium on all $832$ non-associative squares in 3D and on all squares in 2D, where the ring-radius ratio $r_2/r_1=\sqrt{5}$ bounds the resultant below by the Pell convergent $9/4\approx\sqrt{5}$. By length--weight duality, balance is restored via tip weights $\mathbf{w}^*>\mathbf{0}$ on $S^2$ or power-law spoke scaling ($r^{\alpha^*}$ in 2D and $(\mathbf{V}_3)_z=0$ in 3D). In 3D rotation, equal point masses make every semi-magic square an axisymmetric top with spherical-top transition $\lambda_{\mathrm{iso}}=(n^2+1)^{-1/2}$, whereas entry masses $m_{ij}=s_{ij}$ expose the quadrupole $Q_{xy}=\sum z_{ij}x_jy_i$, triggering $180^\circ$ Dzhanibekov flips on $824$ squares. Passing to the uniform solid hull $\mathcal{G}_0(S)$ shifts the centroid off $O$ on $829$ squares; re-engaging the opposing core $\mathcal{G}_1(S)$ restores balance via two-density inclusions, nested wireframes, or the $K_{n^2}$ strut network, while all $880$ hulls unfold into non-overlapping nets with $f_0-1$ glue tabs. Finally, $\lambda=1/5$ stabilizes $74.5\%$ of facets on a table, and alternating $\mathcal{G}_\lambda(S)$ with its mirror twin $\mathcal{G}_\lambda(r^2\overline{S})=-\mathcal{G}_\lambda(S)$ locks chiral blocks into a vertical tower.

papers.title: GC-MoE: Overlapping Expert-Parallel Token Dispatch with FP8/FP4 Grouped GEMM via CUDA Green Contexts
papers.abstract: Under expert parallelism, mixture-of-experts (MoE) layers pay all-to-all token dispatch, grouped GEMMs, and a combine step in every layer. In decode each rank holds only 1-256 tokens: dispatch latency and weight traffic dominate while tensor-core utilization is inherently low. In fused operators such as DeepGEMM's Mega MoE, dispatch and computation overlap only by sharing every SM: dispatch warps compete with TMA/MMA and epilogue warps for registers, shared memory, and issue slots; every phase shares one CTA resource budget, synchronization spans the whole SM array, and every replay ends with a workspace-clean pass and a cross-rank barrier. We present GC-MoE, an open-source FP8/FP4 MoE inference operator for NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell GPUs that uses CUDA Green Contexts to split the device into a small communication partition and a large compute partition. Each role gets its own kernel, resource budget, and synchronization domain, so dispatch and GEMM tune independently. A three-node CUDA Graph (four on Hopper with fused shared experts) launches the dispatch and grouped-GEMM kernels as concurrent roots; a token-ring handshake starts computation on the first filled ring blocks, and double-buffered receive counters remove the trailing cross-rank barrier between replays. The compute partition runs operand-swapped tcgen05 block-scaled MMA on Blackwell and register-A WGMMA with in-register FP4 decoding on Hopper, with fused SwiGLU, requantization, and optional shared experts. On 8 H20 GPUs GC-MoE accelerates DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode by 1.188x on average on both the routed and shared-expert suites (peaks 1.296x and 1.353x); on 8 B300 GPUs it accelerates GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash by 1.106x (1.123x with fused shared experts, peak 1.209x), beating Mega MoE at all 54 measured points at matched accuracy. GC-MoE reserves only 20 of 148 SMs on B300 for dispatch.

authors.name: Tao Lan
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Torsion, valley holonomy, and Berry phases of quasiparticles encircling dislocations and defect complexes in graphene
papers.abstract: We investigate the geometric phase acquired by low-energy quasiparticles encircling defects in graphene. Following Anandan, this phase is the holonomy of the Poincare connection; its translational part couples momentum to torsion, giving $P_a\int T^a$. In the Katanaev-Volovich theory, dislocation torsion is confined to the defect core. For graphene, the relevant momentum is $\hbar(\tau_3\KK+\mathbf q)$. We show that an isolated dislocation yields a topological valley factor $e^{\mp2\pi i/3}$ when its Burgers vector $\bb$ lies outside the $\sqrt3\times\sqrt3$ superlattice, together with a dispersive factor $e^{-i\mathbf q\cdot\bb}$ for every nonzero $\bb$. The topological factor recovers the lattice result of Mesaros et al. as a torsion-flux phase; 4-8 dislocations retain only the dispersive contribution. Composing Volterra elements gives the holonomy of defect complexes. At zero net Frank angle, it depends only on the net Burgers vector. The valley flux obeys a three-coloring rule: pentagons and heptagons contribute according to their Kekule site color, whereas squares and octagons do not. Atomic models confirm that ring content alone does not fix the phase: a 5-8-5 core is invisible as a divacancy or as a dislocation with $|\bb|=\sqrt3a$, but carries flux $\pm1/3$ for $\bb=2\mathbf a_1$. The torsion trace produces no geometric phase: its vector coupling violates time-reversal symmetry, while the allowed axial coupling causes only anisotropic short-range scattering.

papers.title: Reasoning is topologically simple
papers.abstract: We formulate and investigate the hypothesis that reasoning text has simpler co-occurrence topology than non-reasoning text, and that higher-quality reasoning has simpler co-occurrence topology than lower-quality reasoning. We discuss and test applications to AI safety and AI evaluation.

papers.title: The Characteristic Initial Value Problem for the 3D Compressible Euler Equations
papers.abstract: We prove local existence and uniqueness, propagation of Sobolev regularity, and continuation criteria results for the characteristic initial value problem for the 3D compressible Euler equations. This is the Cauchy problem with initial data given on a pair of transversally intersecting (acoustically) null hypersurfaces. The region of existence in our main theorem is a future-neighborhood of the union of the data null hypersurfaces, where the size of the neighborhood depends on various norms of the data as well as the structure of the data null hypersurfaces. We allow for any equation of state with positive sound speed, and we do not make any symmetry, irrotationality, or isentropicity assumptions. Our analysis relies on the geometric formulation of the flow derived in [Speck19], which decomposes the equations into a "wave-part" coupled to a "transport-div-curl" part. Compared to Rendall's celebrated solution of the characteristic initial value problem for wave equations [Rendall90], substantial new ideas are needed to handle the fact that the compressible Euler equations are more complicated than pure wave equations.

papers.title: StepX-OPD: Rethinking Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation in Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: A deployable text-to-image diffusion model must hold several capabilities at once, such as instruction following, text rendering and human preference, and must sample in a few steps. Capabilities and few-step sampling are built in separate stages: a full-step model first consolidates capabilities through multi-teacher on-policy distillation, then serves as a fixed teacher for step distillation. Every full-step model we evaluate scores lower once compressed, and the second stage cannot begin until the first finishes. We introduce StepX-OPD, which merges the two stages: one student acquires every capability while learning to sample in a few steps, so frozen specialists supervise it on the states its own rollout visits rather than on a longer trajectory it never runs. Because a decomposition of the rollout's KL weights velocity mismatch most heavily near the clean end, we also regress the student's velocity on the low-noise part of the rollout. Separately, we find that capability integration makes models write prompt words into images on prompts that never asked for text, and we give a variant that lowers it. We evaluate on SD3.5-Medium and FLUX.1-dev across instruction following, text rendering, image quality and human preference. On both architectures, StepX-OPD attains the highest normalized average score among the four-step methods compared and exceeds the forty-step Flow-OPD model, and on SD3.5-Medium it trains with about 37% fewer GPU-hours than sequential DiffusionOPD followed by step distillation.

papers.title: qLevelPlace: A Level-Based Placement Framework for RSFQ Circuits
papers.abstract: Rapid Single Flux Quantum (RSFQ) logic can operate at ultra-high clock frequencies; however, its physical design is complicated by explicit splitter trees and deep gate-level pipelines in which every logic gate is clocked. To address this challenge, we present qLevelPlace, a level-based placement framework for RSFQ circuits. We separate gate and splitter placement into two stages to better support levelguided gate-to-row assignment and use a timing-aware quadratic cost function to penalize long interconnects. Experiments on the benchmark circuits show that, on average, qLevelPlace achieves a $2.65\times$ higher clock frequency and a 51% reduction in layout area compared with the state-of-the-art RSFQ placer qPlace.

papers.title: Spatial and Temporal Super-Resolution and Denoising of Intracardiac 4D Flow MRI
papers.abstract: Intracardiac flow is driven by complex, and time-varying cardiac motion and interaction with the heart valves, producing complex flow features that may provide valuable information for disease diagnosis and treatment planning. 4D Flow MRI enables non-invasive, time-resolved measurement of three-dimensional cardiovascular velocity fields. However, substantial noise and limited spatial and temporal resolution limit its ability to accurately resolve flow features. We propose 4D-MRAR (4D Magnetic Resonance Augmented Reconstruction), a deep learning (DL) method to super-resolve and denoise 4D Flow MRI data. Unlike prior DL methods that train and infer on static vascular regions, our method predicts intracardiac flow within hearts undergoing large deformation. Moreover, it uniquely allows for simultaneous super-resolution in 3D space and time. The method combines a residual convolutional neural network, a recurrent neural network, and an implicit neural field to predict high-resolution velocity and pressure fields while efficiently enforcing the governing equations of fluid flow during training. Trained on a synthetic dataset obtained from computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of left ventricle (LV) flow, our method generalizes to synthetic whole-heart 4D flow MRI data, and demonstrated promising performance on real 4D Flow MRI. The produced super-resolved flow fields exhibit significantly improved accuracy and greater consistency with the governing equations of blood flow compared with prior methods.

papers.title: Reference-Beam-Assisted Perturbation-Resistant Imaging Through A Single Multimode Fiber
papers.abstract: Multimode fiber (MMF) imaging is highly sensitive to mechanical perturbations, which alter modal coupling and disrupt the speckle-to-target mapping. Here, we propose a reference-beam-assisted method for image reconstruction across multiple fiber configurations. An independent reference beam propagates through the same MMF as the imaging signal without target modulation, providing target-independent transmission-state information through its speckle patterns without requiring a separate configuration-sensing structure. A neural network jointly processes the signal and reference speckles to reconstruct target images. Experiments with MNIST and Fashion-MNIST across 10 fiber configurations demonstrate improved reconstruction quality, faster training convergence, and more accurate configuration identification. Further evaluation across 40 configurations confirms the reconstruction benefit of reference-beam assistance over a larger set of perturbed fiber states. These results provide a foundation for developing perturbation-adaptive MMF imaging systems for flexible endoscopy and minimally invasive optical diagnostics.

papers.title: A Bayesian Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg Model for Real-Time EEG Phase Estimation
papers.abstract: Real-time phase estimation on stimulus-aligned transient EEG is critical for closed-loop neuromodulation systems targeting the theta-band, yet most real-time phase estimation methods have been developed and validated on resting-state, high-fidelity signals in the alpha band. Recent work has pursued deep learning architectures, while individualized classical bandpass filter tuning remains underexplored. This study characterizes the spectral and temporal properties of non-anticipative bandpass filtering and demonstrates the performance gains achieved through individualized tuning. We present a Bayesian-Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg (BOB) model evaluated on EEG recorded during peripheral vibrotactile stimulation of the left median nerve (theta, N=20 healthy subjects) and on resting-state recordings from the Max Planck Institute's LEMON dataset (alpha, N=20 healthy subjects). BOB was benchmarked against the Deep Dual-Branch Complex Neural Network (DBCNN), EEG Phase Prediction Network (EPN), Phastimate, and Phase Estimation with Autoregressive Padding (PEAP) under matched testing conditions: channel selection, individualized optimization, evaluation time points, and an offline reference phase obtained through zero-phase filtering and the Hilbert transform. Under these testing conditions, BOB achieved matched or better performance than these models at a fraction of the calibration time.

papers.title: Interaction-driven Weyl superfluids from topologically trivial bands in an optical Raman lattice
papers.abstract: We propose a scheme to realize Weyl superfluidity from topologically trivial bands in the strongly correlated regime of a three-dimensional optical Raman lattice. The scheme builds on a pairing mechanism arising from the interplay between a large Zeeman splitting and strong Hubbard interaction. Spin-flip hopping suppressed by the large Zeeman detuning is resonantly restored when the attractive Hubbard interaction compensates the energy mismatch, yielding a correlated spin-orbit coupling that depends on the local particle configuration. Combining this density-dependent in-plane spin-orbit coupling with density-dependent spin-conserving interlayer tunneling extends the pairing mechanism to three dimensions. A self-consistent mean-field treatment of the microscopic model yields Weyl superfluids with two, four, or eight nodes, together with fully gapped weak topological superfluids. Tuning the interaction strength and particle filling drives transitions between these phases and controls the number of Weyl nodes. We further propose an experimental implementation with ultracold $^{40}\mathrm{K}$ atoms. Our results highlight density-assisted spin-orbit coupling as a mechanism for realizing Weyl superfluidity in strongly correlated systems.

papers.title: Thermally enhanced magnon-phonon resonance in van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3
papers.abstract: Strong coupling between collective excitations provides a route to controlling quantum states of matter, yet its evolution under thermal fluctuations remains poorly understood. In the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3, strong magnon-phonon coupling is established at low temperatures. At the same time, recent terahertz experiments revealed the counterintuitive stabilization of a long-lived metastable magnetic state with an exceedingly long lifetime of 5 msec at the antiferromagnetic transition, not at the base temperature. This was attributed to a strongly coupled spin-lattice scenario, challenging the conventional wisdom that increased magnetic and thermal fluctuations near TN should be detrimental to the coherent control of a metastable phase. Thus it requires an independent examination for correct understanding. Using high-field Raman spectroscopy, we systematically investigate the temperature evolution of magnon-phonon coupling in FePS3. We observe a pronounced avoided crossing between magnon and phonon modes across a wide range of temperatures and find that the coupling strength remains remarkably robust with increasing temperatures. The zero-field magnon-phonon detuning decreases progressively with warming, driving the system toward resonance and thereby enhancing their hybridization near the transition temperature. This anomalous thermal evolution provides the crucial key to understanding the unusual terahertz-driven states recently reported in FePS3. More broadly, our results highlight van der Waals magnets as a promising platform for strong coupling among collective excitations and for controlling magnetic states through light-matter interactions.

papers.title: DynOSeg: Dynamic Object Segmentation via Motion-Geometry Fusion
papers.abstract: Moving Object Segmentation (MOS) detects and separates dynamic objects from the static background in a video, which plays a fundamental role in dynamic-scene understanding. Most MOS methods rely on pure visual motion cues alone, such as optical flow or point tracks, which is inherently ambiguous due to the compounded camera and object motions as well as motion-induced appearance changes, e.g. shadows and reflections. Naive fusion of additional information such as depth and semantics, however, cannot leverage their complementarity to the fullest extent. We therefore propose DynOSeg, a novel MOS approach that takes on a two-stage fusion structure. DynOSeg first combines a geometry-aware residual map and depth encoding into a geometric representation of motion, delineating camera motions and object dynamics. We then further incorporate semantic features to refine object understanding. We have additionally curated a diverse training corpus including CARLA-MOS, a new synthetic urban-driving dataset for MOS training. Our experiments show that DynOSeg consistently outperforms published state-of-the-art MOS methods across a diverse range of datasets. Our code and pretrained models can be found at https://github.com/ACFR-RPG/DynOSeg

papers.title: Attack-Aware Intrusion Risk Monitoring for Aerial Surveillance via Probabilistic Signal Temporal Logic
papers.abstract: This paper considers online intrusion-risk assessment and graded warning for unmanned aerial vehicles under bounded measurement attacks. To address this problem, we develop a monitoring framework that combines trusted state estimation, attack-aware risk assessment, and probabilistic signal temporal logic (PrSTL). Trusted observations support recursive state estimation, while potentially attacked observations inform integrity testing and intrusion-risk assessment. The key contribution is a confidence-set construction that combines normalized innovation statistics with physical attack bounds to characterize admissible measurement biases. The resulting family of bias-corrected Gaussian posteriors yields an upper bound on the probability of occupying a no-fly zone or its surrounding safety margin. Confidence guarantees and finite-cover numerical certificates quantify the reliability of this risk envelope, which is evaluated with or without an integrity alarm. The PrSTL monitor analyzes the resulting risk sequence to distinguish ordered, persistent, and repeated risk and produces graded warnings with explicit robustness margins and supporting windows. We validate the monitor in flight experiments with a Crazyflie quadrotor tracked by a Vicon motion capture system. Controlled comparisons quantify the contributions of individual monitoring components. Prescribed risk profiles verify the temporal semantics and illustrate how distinct risk patterns produce different warning levels.

papers.title: Correlation Probabilistic Sophistication
papers.abstract: We study binary choice under uncertainty when the comparison between two acts can depend on the joint distribution of their realized outcomes. This motivates correlation probabilistic sophistication (CPS), a subjective reduction principle that extends both probabilistic sophistication and Fishburn's nontransitive subjective expected utility. We show how simultaneous event exchangeability elicits a unique solvable finitely additive subjective probability and reduces binary comparisons of acts to induced joint laws. Under convex range, the induced domain coincides with the full finite joint-law domain, allowing the transfer of correlation-utility representations from risk and, under completeness and Strong Independence, correlation expected utility with a skew-symmetric comparison kernel. Under completeness and transitivity, CPS collapses to ordinary probabilistic sophistication. We further extend the framework to multiple small worlds, allowing correlation sensitivity to vary with the source of uncertainty.

papers.title: Tight Analysis of Randomized Truthful Scheduling: An $(m+1)/2$ Lower Bound
papers.abstract: The Nisan-Ronen conjecture, a central problem in algorithmic game theory, asserts that no deterministic truthful mechanism for makespan minimization on $m$ unrelated machines can achieve an approximation ratio better than $m$. Christodoulou, Koutsoupias, and Kov\'acs resolved it in 2023, but the optimal approximation ratio achievable by randomized truthful mechanisms remained open. Recently, Anastasiadis, Christodoulou, Koutsoupias, Kov\'acs, and Schecker extended techniques from the deterministic proof to establish a $(3/2-\sqrt{2})(m-1)$ lower bound for universally truthful mechanisms with discrete support and gave a universally truthful mechanism with approximation ratio $m/2+o(m)$. For the broader class of truthful-in-expectation (TIE) mechanisms, however, the gap remained large: the best known upper bound was $(m+5)/2$, while the lower bound was only $2-1/m$. We prove a lower bound of $(m+1)/2$, determining the optimal TIE approximation ratio up to an additive constant as $m/2+\Theta(1)$. Our result also improves the leading constant in the lower bound for universally truthful mechanisms from $3/2-\sqrt{2} \approx 0.0858$ to $1/2$. Together with their $m/2+o(m)$ upper bound, our result determines the optimal approximation ratio for universally truthful mechanisms up to lower-order terms.

papers.title: Bang-Bang Correlation Sensitivity: A Local-to-Global Dichotomy for Correlation Preference
papers.abstract: Binary choice under risk can depend on how the alternative outcomes are jointly distributed. We show that in a finite outcome space, continuity, completeness, and betweenness impose a local-to-global restriction on this dependence: indifference between two alternatives with one common marginal distribution, however their outcomes are jointly distributed, implies correlation insensitivity for all lotteries supported on the same outcomes. In the correlation-sensitive case, these three axioms alone characterize correlation weighted utility, which combines statewise comparisons with a bilinear function of the marginal lotteries. In the correlation-insensitive case, an additional projective independence axiom yields Fishburn's (1982) skew-symmetric bilinear representation. Strong independence reduces correlation weighted utility to Lanzani's (2022) correlation expected utility representation. We extend the correlation-sensitive characterization to finitely supported lotteries on general metrizable outcome spaces. The resulting framework distinguishes correlation effects from departures from classical independence, and yields testable restrictions linking choices between identically distributed lotteries to correlated Allais behavior.

papers.title: Uniqueness of scalar-flat ALE K\"ahler metrics
papers.abstract: We study uniqueness of scalar-flat K\"ahler metrics in a fixed K\"ahler class on an asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) K\"ahler manifold, assuming only differentiated $o(1)$ decay to a fixed Euclidean metric on the end. In complex dimension $n\geq2$, under suitable polynomial decay of the reference metric, we prove that the relative Mabuchi functional is finite, continuous, and convex along weak geodesics whose endpoint potentials satisfy $u=O(r^{-\gamma})$, $\gamma>2n-4$, together with the corresponding derivative estimates. Combining this convexity with the analysis of the Lichnerowicz operator in weighted spaces, we obtain uniqueness by a perturbation argument. Decay improvement and comparison of the asymptotic charts produce a global potential with the required decay for the difference of the two cohomologous scalar-flat K\"ahler forms. The argument also extends to asymptotically conical K\"ahler metrics approaching a fixed Ricci-flat K\"ahler cone under prescribed decay assumptions.

papers.title: Separating Common and Unique Directions for Data-Free Model Merging
papers.abstract: Model merging combines multiple fine-tuned models without additional training, and arithmetic methods have emerged as a simple yet effective way to merge models without data. However, existing arithmetic methods treat task vectors in parameter space and apply a single element-wise rule to directions that can differ in mergeability. In a shared directional basis, we find a consistent two-regime structure: a low-dispersion common bulk shared across tasks and a high-dispersion task-dominated tail that carries disproportionate energy. These findings motivate Common--Unique Subspace Decomposition (CUSD), a data-free pre-merging method that separates task vectors into common and unique directional components, merges the common components with downstream arithmetic operator, and retains unique residuals separately. Experiments across $11$ base models, four model families, and four arithmetic-based merging operators show that CUSD improves 42 of 44 model--operator combinations and achieves up to 22.5% improvement over the corresponding baselines. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/stwang666/CUSD

papers.title: Toward Generalized LEO Channel Prediction: A Rapid Adaptation Time-Frequency Mamba Framework
papers.abstract: Accurate channel state information (CSI) prediction is pivotal for enhancing system capacity in low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite-terrestrial communications within the sixth-generation vision of global ubiquitous connectivity. However, the extreme mobility of LEO satellites, coupled with significant propagation delays, induces severe channel aging. Existing deep learning (DL) methods often struggle with non-stationary dynamics or generalize poorly across diverse global geographies. To address these challenges, we design the Evo-TFMamba, which is an evolutionary framework integrating time-frequency selective Mamba blocks with meta-learning for generalized CSI prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed Evo-TFMamba performs adaptive prediction according to the geographic coverage of LEO satellites. Meanwhile, it significantly enhances the model's generalization ability, particularly when faced with unseen channel environments in LEO satellite communication.

papers.title: Fitting Resonant Exoplanets Orbits. I. Properties and Applications of Fixed-Point Orbits
papers.abstract: Intact chains of mean-motion resonances may preserve information about the formation and early dynamical evolution of multiplanet systems. Although most mature multiplanet systems are non-resonant, the resonant fraction may have been substantially higher at young ages. Establishing whether exoplanet data are consistent with a resonant configuration is often challenging because the planetary orbits must be sufficiently well constrained. Moreover, while resonance configurations promote stability, standard orbital fitting methods do not impose such a dynamical constraint, with stability tested only a posteriori. As the first step in a series of papers aimed at favoring stable orbital solutions during the fitting process, we develop a method that restricts solutions to stable fixed-point orbits (fPOs)---coplanar, exactly periodic configurations associated with resonant dynamics. We show that dissipative evolution drive resonant systems toward an fPO state, motivating for fPO-constrained fitting for those planet systems that have avoided large-scale dynamical rearrangements since formation. The fPO model greatly reduces the number of free parameters and yields stable solutions by construction. We determine the best-fitting fPos through $\chi^2$ minimization and apply the method to astrometric data for the directly imaged PDS 70 and HR 8799 systems and to radial-velocity data for GJ 876. For HR 8799 we independently recover a previously reported resonant solution, illustrating the fidelity of our method. For PDS 70 we find solutions fall in two groups, with the group where the outer planet c mass exceeds planet b more aligned with previous measurements. Finally, For GJ 876 our fPO fit is on par with previous unconstrained fitting, which strengthens the case that its planets reside deep in resonance.

papers.title: Beyond Token Representations: Explicit Visual Object Grounding for Video Reasoning Segmentation
papers.abstract: Video Reasoning Segmentation (VRS) aims to infer and segment target objects specified by reasoning queries in videos. Existing methods typically first infer the target and generate a few segmentation tokens for it, which are then fed into a mask decoder for mask prediction. However, such segmentation tokens tend to be both semantically monotonous and spatially ambiguous, making them largely insufficient to represent the target to guide mask prediction. In this paper, we propose an explicit visual object grounding framework for VRS. Specifically, we first propose a spatial-aware prompt generation and refinement scheme, in which we query a multimodal large language model to generate explicit spatial prompts (i.e., bounding box and point set) for the target and then refine them through multi-step dialogue. Furthermore, we introduce a query diversification and alignment module to generate auxiliary queries that describe the same target from different perspectives. We then enforce cross-query consistency between their predicted spatial prompts to alleviate the training bias caused by query limitations. Finally, we select several reliable frames using a prompt-based keyframe selection strategy to support mask decoding and propagation. Extensive experiments on eight datasets demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The code is available at https://github.com/viscom-tongji/EVOG.

papers.title: On the Irreducibility of Locally Analytic Vectors in Certain Banach Representations of $D^\times$
papers.abstract: We investigate the structure of locally analytic representations of $p$-adic groups, and establish a sufficient condition for the irreducibility of locally analytic vectors in certain Banach representations of $D^\times$, where $D$ is the quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. As an application, we prove that $\mathrm{JL}(\rho)^{\mathrm{an}}/\mathrm{JL}(\rho)^{1\text{-}\mathrm{alg}}$ is a topologically irreducible locally analytic representation of $D^\times$ under certain genericity conditions on $\rho$. Here $\mathrm{JL}(\rho)$ is the $\rho(-1)$-multiplicity space in the image of $\Pi(\rho)$ under Scholze's functor, and $\Pi(\rho)$ is the representation associated to $\rho$ by the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.

papers.title: Predicting protein structures at any folding stage from sequence
papers.abstract: Protein structure predictors reliably identify native conformations, but do not describe the continuum connecting unfolded ensembles to folded states. Here we present FoldScape, a sequence-conditioned deep learning framework that generates C$\alpha$ conformational ensembles at a specified folding fraction $Q$. FoldScape reconstructs three-dimensional chains through hierarchical, sliding-window regressions of one-dimensional inter-residue distances, followed by chain assembly and sampling with a rectified-flow decoder. It is trained on multi-scale coarse-grained folding trajectories and all-atom mechanical-unfolding trajectories. Across 20 human proteins (36-857 residues), at matched sample size, FoldScape covers about an order of magnitude more of the folding coordinate than seed-varied AlphaFold 3 ensembles, robustly across proteins, order parameters and binning choices. AlphaFold 3 better anchors the immediate native vicinity, which FoldScape does not reach, making the approaches complementary. FoldScape reconstruction accuracy remains approximately constant along $Q$, from collapsed coil to near-native globule, rather than deteriorating away from the native state. A stride-one crop-and-superpose scheme extends inference to chains several times longer than a single chain-level forward pass. We also show that training trajectories resolve mechanical unfolding at residue resolution, that elongation-conditioned ensembles exhibit reproducible continuous observables across pulling velocities, and that partially unfolded chains form geometrically coherent segments. FoldScape thus combines broad coverage of folding stages with stable reconstruction accuracy, without per-protein simulation.
